sentences.zh: 禮十六

translations.literal: Rites 16
translations.idiomatic: Rites 16

sentences.zh: 〈（嘉禮四）〉

translations.literal: (Auspicious Rites, Part Four)
translations.idiomatic: (Auspicious Rites, Part Four)

sentences.zh: ○宴饗遊觀賜酺

translations.literal: ○ Banquets, Outings, and Bestowed Communal Feasts
translations.idiomatic: Banquets, Outings, and Bestowed Communal Feasts

sentences.zh: 宴饗之設，所以訓恭儉、示惠慈也。

translations.literal: The institution of banquets is to train reverence and frugality and to display kindness and compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Banquets were instituted to cultivate reverence and frugality and to display kindness and compassion.

sentences.zh: 宋制，嘗以春秋之季仲及聖節、郊祀、籍田禮畢，巡幸還京，凡國有大慶皆大 宴，遇大災、大劄則罷。

translations.literal: Under the Song system, grand banquets were customarily held in the middle months of spring and autumn, on imperial birthdays, after suburban sacrifice and plowing-the-sacred-field rites were completed, and when the emperor returned to the capital after tours; whenever the state had a great celebration a grand banquet was held, and when there was a great disaster or a great imperial mourning edict they were canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song regulations, grand banquets were usually held in the middle months of spring and autumn, on imperial birthdays, after suburban sacrifice and the sacred-field plowing, and when the emperor returned from tour; any great national celebration called for a grand banquet, while great disasters or major mourning edicts suspended them.

sentences.zh: 天聖後，大宴率於集英殿，次宴紫宸殿，小宴垂拱殿，若特旨則不拘常制。

translations.literal: After the Tiansheng era, grand banquets were usually in the Hall of Collected Elegance, secondary banquets in the Hall of Purple Felicity, and minor banquets in the Hall of Bowed Reverence; if there was a special edict, the regular rules were not binding.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tiansheng period, grand banquets were usually held in the Hall of Collected Elegance, secondary banquets in the Hall of Purple Felicity, and minor banquets in the Hall of Bowed Reverence; special edicts could override the usual arrangements.

sentences.zh: 凡大宴，有司預於殿庭設山樓排場，為群仙隊仗、六番進貢、九 龍五鳳之狀，司天雞唱樓於其側。

translations.literal: For every grand banquet, the relevant offices beforehand set up in the court a mountain-pavilion stage with formations of the Immortals in procession, the six tribute missions, and the forms of the Nine Dragons and Five Phoenixes; the Office of Heaven set up a cock-crow tower at its side.
translations.idiomatic: Before each grand banquet, the responsible offices erected in the courtyard a mountain-pavilion stage featuring Immortal processions, the six tribute missions, and Nine Dragons and Five Phoenixes; the Office of Heaven placed a cock-crow tower beside it.

sentences.zh: 殿上陳錦繡帷帟，垂香球，設銀香獸前檻內，藉以文茵，設禦茶床、酒器於殿東北楹，群臣盞斝於殿下幕屋。

translations.literal: On the hall were displayed brocade curtains and canopies, with incense balls hanging down; inside the front railing were set silver incense beasts on patterned mats; at the northeast pillar of the hall were set the imperial tea table and wine vessels, and the ministers’ cups and goblets in the tent-houses below the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade curtains and canopies hung in the hall, incense balls suspended above; silver incense beasts stood inside the front railing on patterned mats; the imperial tea table and wine vessels were placed at the hall’s northeast pillar, while ministers’ cups and goblets were kept in tent-houses below.

sentences.zh: 設宰相、使相、樞密 使、知樞密院、參知政事、樞密副使、同知樞密院、宣徽使、三師、三公、僕射、尚書丞郎、學士、直學士、御史大夫、中丞、三司使、給、諫、舍人、節度使、兩 使留後、觀察、團練使、待制、宗室、遙郡團練使、刺史、上將軍、統軍、軍廂指揮使坐於殿上，文武四品以上、知雜御史、郎中、郎將、禁軍都虞候坐於朵殿，自 餘升朝官、諸軍副都頭以上、諸蕃進奉使、諸道進奉軍將以上分於兩廡。

translations.literal: The chief counselor, commissioner with ministerial powers, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner, director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, vice grand councilor, vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, associate director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, commissioner of the Palace Domestic Service, the Three Preceptors, the Three Excellencies, the Pushe, vice ministers and directors of the Six Ministries, academicians, direct academicians, censor-in-chief, vice censor-in-chief, commissioner of the Three Departments, remonstrance and memorial officials, secretariat drafters, military commissioners, two commissioners on leave, observation and training commissioners, awaiting appointment, imperial clansmen, distant prefecture training commissioners, prefects, senior generals, army supervisors, commanders of army wings were seated in the hall; civil and military officials of the fourth rank and above, supervising censors, directors, commandants, and commanders of the palace guards were seated in the side hall; the remaining court officials, deputy commanders of the various armies and above, tribute envoys from the various foreign states, and military commissioners presenting tribute from the various circuits were distributed in the two wings.
translations.idiomatic: Seated in the main hall were the chief counselor, commissioners with ministerial powers, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioners and deputies, vice grand councilors, Palace Domestic Service commissioner, Three Preceptors, Three Excellencies, Pushe, vice ministers, academicians, censor-in-chief, Three Departments commissioner, remonstrance and memorial officials, secretariat drafters, military commissioners, officials on leave, observation and training commissioners, awaiting appointment, imperial clansmen, distant prefects, prefects, senior generals, army supervisors, and wing commanders; civil and military officials of the fourth rank and above, supervising censors, directors, commandants, and palace guard commanders sat in the side hall; all other court officials, deputy army commanders and above, foreign tribute envoys, and circuit tribute commissioners were placed in the two wings.

sentences.zh: 宰臣、使相坐以繡墩；

translations.literal: The chief counselor and commissioners with ministerial powers sat on embroidered cushions;
translations.idiomatic: Chief counselors and commissioners with ministerial powers sat on embroidered cushions;

sentences.zh: 〈（曲宴行幸用杌子。）〉

translations.literal: (At informal banquets on imperial tours, backless stools were used.)
translations.idiomatic: (On tours, informal banquets used backless stools.)

sentences.zh: 參知政事以下用二蒲墩，加罽兟；

translations.literal: Those from the vice grand councilor down used two rush cushions with felt covers added;
translations.idiomatic: From the vice grand councilor down, officials used two rush cushions with felt covers;

sentences.zh: 〈（曲宴，樞 密使、副並同。）〉

translations.literal: (At informal banquets, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner and deputy were the same.)
translations.idiomatic: (At informal banquets, the Bureau commissioner and deputy followed the same rule.)

sentences.zh: 軍都指揮使以上用一蒲墩；

translations.literal: Army commanders and above used one rush cushion;
translations.idiomatic: Army commanders and above used one rush cushion;

sentences.zh: 自朵殿而下皆緋緣氈條席。

translations.literal: from the side hall down, all used crimson-bordered felt strip mats.
translations.idiomatic: from the side hall downward all used crimson-bordered felt strip mats.

sentences.zh: 殿上器用金，餘以銀。

translations.literal: Vessels on the hall used gold; the rest used silver.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels in the hall were gold; elsewhere silver.

sentences.zh: 其日，樞密使以下先起居訖，當侍立者升殿。

translations.literal: On that day, from the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner down they first paid their respects; those who were to attend standing then ascended the hall.
translations.idiomatic: That day, from the Bureau commissioner down officials paid respects first; those assigned to stand attendance then entered the hall.

sentences.zh: 宰相率百官入，宣徽、 閣門通唱，致辭訖，宰相升殿進酒，各就坐，酒九行。

translations.literal: The chief counselor led the hundred officials in; the Palace Domestic Service and Gate Office announced in chorus; when the address of congratulation was finished, the chief counselor ascended the hall to present wine; each took his seat; wine was served in nine rounds.
translations.idiomatic: The chief counselor led the officials in; the Palace Domestic Service and Gate Office called the ceremony; after the congratulatory address the counselor ascended to present wine; everyone took his seat; nine rounds of wine followed.

sentences.zh: 每上舉酒，群臣立侍，次宰相、次百官舉酒；

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor raised his cup, the ministers stood in attendance; next the chief counselor, then the hundred officials raised their cups;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor raised his cup, ministers stood in attendance; then the chief counselor, then all officials raised theirs;

sentences.zh: 或傳旨命釂，即搢笏起飲，再拜。

translations.literal: or if an edict ordered a toast, they then inserted their tablets, rose to drink, and bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: or if an edict ordered a toast, they inserted their tablets, rose, drank, and bowed again.

sentences.zh: 〈（曲宴多令不拜。）〉

translations.literal: (At informal banquets they were often ordered not to bow.)
translations.idiomatic: (Informal banquets often waived bowing.)

sentences.zh: 或上壽朝 會，止令滿酌，不勸。

translations.literal: Or at birthday congratulations or court assemblies, they were only ordered to fill their cups and were not urged to drink.
translations.idiomatic: At birthday congratulations or court assemblies they were told only to fill their cups, not urged to drink further.

sentences.zh: 中飲更衣，賜花有差。

translations.literal: At the mid-banquet they changed clothes; conferred flowers differed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-banquet they changed dress; conferred flowers varied by rank.

sentences.zh: 宴訖，蹈舞拜謝而退。

translations.literal: When the banquet ended, they performed the treading dance, bowed in thanks, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the banquet ended, they performed the treading dance, bowed in thanks, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 建隆元年，大宴於廣德殿，酒九行而罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianlong, a grand banquet was held in the Hall of Broad Virtue; wine in nine rounds and it ended.
translations.idiomatic: Jianlong 1: a grand banquet in the Hall of Broad Virtue ended after nine rounds of wine.

sentences.zh: 乾德元年十一月，南郊禮成，大宴廣德 殿，謂之飲福。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Qiande, when the suburban sacrifice was completed, a grand banquet was held in the Hall of Broad Virtue, called Drinking the Blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Qiande 1, eleventh month: after the suburban sacrifice, a grand banquet in the Hall of Broad Virtue was called Drinking the Blessing.

sentences.zh: 是後三年，開寶三年、五年、六年、七年、八年，並設秋宴於大明殿，以長春節在二月故也。

translations.literal: Three years thereafter, in the third, fifth, sixth, seventh, and eighth years of Kaibao, autumn banquets were all set in the Hall of Great Brightness, because the Birthday of Everlasting Spring fell in the second month.
translations.idiomatic: For the next three years, and in Kaibao 3, 5, 6, 7, and 8, autumn banquets were held in the Hall of Great Brightness because the Birthday of Everlasting Spring fell in the second month.

sentences.zh: 太平興國之後，止設春宴，在大明者十一，在含光者 六。

translations.literal: After the Taiping Xingguo period, only spring banquets were held—eleven in the Hall of Great Brightness and six in the Hall of Containing Light.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiping Xingguo, only spring banquets remained—eleven in the Hall of Great Brightness and six in the Hall of Containing Light.

sentences.zh: 宴日，親王、樞密使副、宣徽、三司使、駙馬都尉皆侍立，軍校自龍武四廂都指揮使以上立於庭。

translations.literal: On banquet days, imperial princes, the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner and deputy, the Palace Domestic Service commissioner, the Three Departments commissioner, and the imperial sons-in-law all stood in attendance; military officers from the four wings of the Dragon Martial Guard commander up stood in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: On banquet days imperial princes, Bureau commissioner and deputy, Palace Domestic Service commissioner, Three Departments commissioner, and imperial sons-in-law stood in attendance; officers from the four Dragon Martial wings upward stood in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 其宴契丹使亦於崇德殿，但近臣及刺史、郎中而上預焉。

translations.literal: When entertaining Khitan envoys, it was also in the Hall of Honored Virtue, but only close ministers and those from prefect up and director up participated.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys were also entertained in the Hall of Honored Virtue, but only close ministers and officials from prefect and director rank upward attended.

sentences.zh: 淳化四年正月，以南郊禮成，大宴含光殿，直史館陳靖上言：「古之饗宴者，所以省禍福而觀威儀也。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year of Chunhua, because the suburban sacrifice was completed, a grand banquet was held in the Hall of Containing Light; Chen Jing of the Direct Historiography Office submitted a memorial: “Banquets of antiquity were to survey fortune and misfortune and observe ritual bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Chunhua 4, first month: after the suburban sacrifice a grand banquet was held in the Hall of Containing Light; Chen Jing of the Direct Historiography Office wrote: “Ancient feasts surveyed fortune and misfortune and displayed ritual decorum.

sentences.zh: 故宴以禮成，賓以賢序，《風》、《雅》之作，茲為盛焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the banquet follows ritual completion, guests are ordered by worth, and the compositions in the 《Airs》 and 《Eulogies》—here is their fullness.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the feast follows completed rites, guests are ranked by merit, and the pieces in the 《Airs》 and 《Eulogies》 mark the height of such ceremony.

sentences.zh: 伏見近年內殿賜宴，群臣當坐於朵殿、兩廊者，拜舞方畢，趨馳就席，品列之序，糾紛無別。

translations.literal: I observe that in recent years at inner-palace bestowed banquets, when ministers who should sit in the side hall and the two wings had finished bowing and dancing, they hurried to their seats; the order of ranks was confused without distinction.
translations.idiomatic: In recent inner-palace banquets, ministers assigned to the side hall and wings finished their bows and then rushed to their seats, so rank order collapsed into confusion.

sentences.zh: 及至尊舉爵，群臣起立，先後不整，俯仰失節。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven raised his goblet, the ministers rose to their feet; the sequence was not orderly, and in bowing and rising they lost propriety.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor raised his goblet, ministers rose in disorder, bowing and rising without proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 欲望自今令有司預依品 位告諭，其有逾越班次、拜起失節、喧嘩過甚者，並令糾舉。

translations.literal: I desire that from now on the relevant offices beforehand announce according to rank; those who overstep their place in the sequence, err in bowing and rising, or are excessively noisy should all be reported and disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that hereafter the responsible offices announce seating by rank in advance; anyone who oversteps place, errs in bowing, or is excessively noisy should be reported and disciplined.

sentences.zh: 又惟飫賜之典，以寵武夫，大烹之餘，故為盛饌。

translations.literal: Moreover, the bestowal feast is to favor military men; after the great cooking there is therefore a lavish spread.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the bestowal feast honors military men; after the great cooking comes an especially lavish spread.

sentences.zh: 計一飯所費，可數人之屬厭，而將校輩或至終宴之 時，尚有欲炙之色，蓋執事者失於察視，不及潔豐而使然也。

translations.literal: The cost of a single meal could satisfy several persons, yet commanders and the like sometimes even at the end of the banquet still showed a desire for roast meat—because those in charge failed in oversight and did not make the offerings ample and clean, causing this.
translations.idiomatic: A single meal could feed several men, yet some commanders even at the banquet’s end still looked hungry for roast meat—because overseers had not ensured ample, clean provisions.

sentences.zh: 伏望並申嚴製。」

translations.literal: I humbly hope this too may be strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that this too be strictly enforced.

sentences.zh: 至道元年三月，御史中丞李昌齡亦言：「廣宴之設，以均飫賜，得齒高會，宜乎盡 禮。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Zhidao, Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Changling also said: “The setting of a broad banquet is to equalize the bestowal feast; to attain a high assembly should mean full observance of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidao 1, third month: Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Changling also said: “Broad banquets equalize the bestowal feast; those of rank who attend should observe full ritual.

sentences.zh: 而有位之士，鮮克致恭，當糾其不恪。

translations.literal: Yet men of position seldom achieve reverence; their lack of respect should be disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: Yet men of position seldom show due respect; their negligence should be disciplined.

sentences.zh: 又供事禁庭，當定員數，籍姓名以謹其出入。

translations.literal: Moreover, those who serve in the forbidden precinct should have fixed numbers; register names to tighten their coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Those serving in the forbidden precinct should have fixed numbers; register names to control entry and exit.

sentences.zh: 酒殽之司，或虧精潔，望分命中使巡察。」

translations.literal: In the offices of wine and meat, sometimes refinement and cleanliness are lacking; I hope eunuch commissioners may be assigned to inspect in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Wine and meat offices sometimes lack refinement; assign rotating eunuch inspectors.

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: Both were approved.
translations.idiomatic: Both proposals were approved.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年 二月，大宴含光殿，自是始備設春秋大宴。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Xianping, a grand banquet was held in the Hall of Containing Light; from this spring and autumn grand banquets were fully instituted.
translations.idiomatic: Xianping 3, second month: a grand banquet in the Hall of Containing Light; spring and autumn grand banquets were fully instituted from this point.

sentences.zh: 五年，御史臺言：「大宴，起居舍人、司諫、正言、三院使、御史並坐於殿廊，望自今移升朵殿，自餘依舊。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year, the Censorate said: “At grand banquets, the diarist, remonstrance officials, rectifiers, the three institute commissioners, and censors all sit in the hall corridors; I hope that from now they may be moved up to the side hall; the rest as before.”
translations.idiomatic: Year 5: the Censorate said: “At grand banquets diarists, remonstrance officials, rectifiers, three-institute commissioners, and censors sit in the hall corridors; move them to the side hall hereafter; the rest unchanged.”

sentences.zh: 十二月， 詔凡內宴，宗正卿令升殿坐，班次依合班儀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, an edict: for all inner banquets, the director of the Imperial Clan Command was to ascend and be seated; place in the ranks followed the Combined Audience regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: for all inner banquets the Imperial Clan director was to ascend and take a seat; seating followed the Combined Audience regulations.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士梁顥請以春秋大宴、小宴、賞花、行幸次為四圖，頒下閣門遵守。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Liang Hao requested that spring grand banquet, minor banquet, flower viewing, and tour sequences be made into four charts and issued to the Gate Office for observance.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Liang Hao asked that spring grand banquet, minor banquet, flower viewing, and tour sequences be drawn in four charts and issued to the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 景德二年九月，詔 曰：「朝會陳儀，衣冠就列，將以訓上下、彰文物，宜慎等威，用符紀律。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Jingde, an edict said: “At court assemblies the rites are displayed, robes and caps take their places—to train superiors and inferiors and manifest cultural objects; rank and dignity should be carefully observed to match discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde 2, ninth month: an edict said: “Court assemblies display ritual; robes and caps take their places to train rank and manifest civilization; dignity must match discipline.

sentences.zh: 況屢頒於條令，宜自顧於典刑。

translations.literal: Moreover, this has been repeatedly promulgated in regulations; one should look to the canonical punishments.
translations.idiomatic: This has been repeatedly promulgated; officials should heed the canonical penalties.

sentences.zh: 稍曆歲時，漸成懈慢。

translations.literal: After some years, slackness gradually arose.
translations.idiomatic: Over the years slackness had gradually set in.

sentences.zh: 特申明製，以儆具僚。

translations.literal: The regulations are specially clarified to warn all officials.
translations.idiomatic: The regulations are now clarified to warn all officials.

sentences.zh: 自今宴會， 宜令御史臺預定位次，各令端肅，不得喧嘩。

translations.literal: From now on at banquets, the Censorate should beforehand fix seating; each should be upright and solemn and must not be noisy.
translations.idiomatic: Hereafter at banquets the Censorate shall fix seating in advance; all must remain solemn and quiet.

sentences.zh: 違者，殿上委大夫、中丞，朵殿委知雜御史、侍御史，廊下委左右巡使，察視彈奏；

translations.literal: Violators: on the hall, entrust to the grand censor and vice censor-in-chief; in the side hall, to the supervising censor and attendant censor; in the corridors, to the left and right patrol commissioners—for inspection and impeachment;
translations.idiomatic: Violators on the hall are reported by the grand censor and vice censor-in-chief; in the side hall by supervising and attendant censors; in the corridors by left and right patrol commissioners;

sentences.zh: 內職殿直以上赴起居、入殿庭行私 禮者，委閣門彈奏；

translations.literal: inner-service officials of palace attendance rank and above who attend audience or enter the hall court to perform private rites are entrusted to the Gate Office for impeachment;
translations.idiomatic: inner-service officials of palace attendance and above who attend audience or perform private rites in the hall court are reported by the Gate Office;

sentences.zh: 其軍員，令殿前侍衛司各差都校一人提轄，但虧失禮容，即送所司勘斷訖奏。

translations.literal: for military personnel, order the Palace Front and Rear Guard Service each to detail one company commander to supervise; whoever lacks ritual bearing is sent to the relevant office for investigation and report when finished.
translations.idiomatic: for military personnel each Palace Guard service shall detail one company commander; anyone lacking proper bearing is sent for investigation and report.

sentences.zh: 仍令閣門、宣徽使互相察舉，敢蔽匿者糾之。」

translations.literal: Still order the Gate Office and Palace Domestic Service commissioner to inspect each other; whoever dares conceal is to be impeached.”
translations.idiomatic: The Gate Office and Palace Domestic Service commissioner shall also inspect each other; concealment is impeachable.”

sentences.zh: 大中 祥符元年十二月，詔宣徽院、御史臺、閣門、殿前馬步軍司，凡內宴臣僚、軍員並祗候使臣等，並以前後儀製曉諭，務令遵稟，違者密具名聞。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict to the Palace Domestic Service, Censorate, Gate Office, and Palace Front and Rear Guard Service: for all inner-banquet civil officials, military personnel, and attendant envoys, instruct them in former and latter ritual models, striving to make them obey; violators are to be secretly reported by name.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong Xiangfu 1, twelfth month: the Palace Domestic Service, Censorate, Gate Office, and Palace Guards were ordered to instruct all inner-banquet officials, soldiers, and attendants in former and current ritual and report violators secretly by name.

sentences.zh: 其軍員有因酒言詞失 次及醉仆者，即先扶出，或遣殿前司量添巡檢軍士護送歸營。

translations.literal: Military personnel who because of wine have disorderly words or fall down drunk are first assisted out, or the Palace Front Service is sent to add patrol soldiers as needed to escort them back to camp.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who grow disorderly or fall drunk are first helped out, or the Palace Front Service adds patrols to escort them to camp.

sentences.zh: 又詔臣僚有托故請假不赴宴者，御史臺糾奏。

translations.literal: Also an edict: civil officials who plead illness and do not attend the banquet—the Censorate shall impeach.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials who falsely plead illness to skip the banquet are impeached by the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年，直集賢院祖士衡言：「大宴將更衣，群臣下 殿，然後更衣，更衣後再坐，則群臣班於殿庭，候上升坐，起居謝賜花，再拜升殿。」

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianxi, Zu Shihang of the Direct Academy said: “Before the grand banquet changes clothes, the ministers descend the hall; only then are clothes changed; after changing clothes and sitting again, the ministers line up in the hall court, wait for the emperor to ascend and sit, pay respects and thank him for the conferred flowers, bow again, and ascend the hall.”
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi 4: Zu Shihang of the Direct Academy said: “Before the mid-banquet change of dress ministers leave the hall; after the emperor returns they line in the courtyard, thank him for flowers, bow twice, and re-enter.”

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖三年，監察御史朱諫言：「伏見大宴，宗室先退，允為得禮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tiansheng of Renzong, Supervising Censor Zhu Jian said: “I observe that at grand banquets the imperial clan withdraws first—this is proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong, Tiansheng 3: Supervising Censor Zhu Jian said: “At grand banquets the imperial clan withdraws first—this is proper.

sentences.zh: 尚有文武臣僚父子、兄弟者，皆預再坐，欲望自今內宴，百官有父子、兄弟、叔侄同赴，再坐時卑者先退。」

translations.literal: There are still civil and military officials who are father and son or brothers, all attending the second seating; I desire that from now at inner banquets, when officials have father and son, brothers, or uncle and nephew attending together, at the second seating the junior withdraws first.”
translations.idiomatic: Yet fathers and sons or brothers among civil and military officials all stay for the second seating; at inner banquets when kin attend together, juniors should withdraw first at the second seating.”

sentences.zh: 慶曆七年，御史言：「凡預大宴並御筵，其所賜花，並須載歸私第，不得更令仆從持戴，違者糾舉。」

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Qingli, the censor said: “All who attend grand banquets and imperial feasts must carry the conferred flowers back to their private residences and must not again have servants hold or wear them; violators are to be impeached.”
translations.idiomatic: Qingli 7: censors said flowers conferred at grand banquets and imperial feasts must be carried home personally, not worn by servants; violators are impeached.”

sentences.zh: 熙寧二年正月，閣門言：「準詔裁定集英殿宴入殿人數：中書二十二人，樞密院三十人，宣徽院八人，親王八人，昭德軍節度使、兼侍中曹佾三人，皇親使相三 人，皇親正刺史已上至節度使並駙馬都尉各一人，翰林司一百七十八人，禦廚六百人，儀鸞司一百五十人，祗候庫二十人，內衣物庫七人，新衣庫七人，內弓箭庫三 人，鈐轄教坊所三人，鍾鼓樓一十六人，禦藥院八人，內物料庫九人，法酒庫一十六人，內酒坊八人，入內內侍省前後行、親事官共五人，皇城司職員手分二人，禦 史台知班一十一人，灑掃親從官人員已下一百人，兩廊覷步親從官四十二人，提舉司勾押官手分三人，提舉火燭巡檢人員一十人，快行親從官一十一人，支散兩省花 後苑造作所工匠等四人，客省承授行首八人，四方館職掌二人，閣門承受行首已下一十八人。」

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year of Xining, the Gate Office said: “According to the edict fixing the number entering the Hall of Collected Elegance banquet: Secretariat 22, Bureau of Military Affairs 30, Palace Domestic Service 8, imperial princes 8, Zhaode Army military commissioner and concurrent Palace Attendant Cao You 3, imperial clansmen with commissioner powers 3, imperial clansmen from regular prefect up to military commissioner and imperial sons-in-law each 1, Hanlin Office 178, Imperial Kitchen 600, Ceremonial Escort Office 150, Attendant Storehouse 20, Inner Garment Storehouse 7, New Garment Storehouse 7, Inner Bow and Arrow Storehouse 3, Supervisory Music Office 3, Bell and Drum Tower 16, Imperial Pharmacy 8, Inner Materials Storehouse 9, Statutory Wine Storehouse 16, Inner Wine Workshop 8, Inner Palace Attendant Service front and rear rows and personal attendants 5 total, Imperial City Service clerks and assistants 2, Censorate session leaders 11, sweeping personal attendants and staff 100, two-corridor step-watching personal attendants 42, Supervisory Office checking clerks 3, fire-candle patrol personnel 10, fast-walking personal attendants 11, distributing two-province flowers, Rear Garden Construction Office artisans 4, Guest Reception Office lead receivers 8, Four Directions Office managers 2, Gate Office receiving leads 18 and below.”
translations.idiomatic: Xining 2, first month: the Gate Office reported the edict fixing Hall of Collected Elegance attendance: Secretariat 22, Bureau of Military Affairs 30, Palace Domestic Service 8, imperial princes 8, Cao You 3, imperial clansmen commissioners 3, clansmen from prefect to commissioner and sons-in-law 1 each, Hanlin Office 178, Imperial Kitchen 600, Ceremonial Escort 150, Attendant Storehouse 20, Inner Garment 7, New Garment 7, Inner Bow Storehouse 3, Music Office 3, Bell Tower 16, Imperial Pharmacy 8, Inner Materials 9, Statutory Wine 16, Inner Wine Workshop 8, Inner Attendant Service 5, Imperial City clerks 2, Censorate leaders 11, sweeping attendants 100, corridor watchers 42, supervisory clerks 3, fire patrols 10, fast attendants 11, flower distributors, Rear Garden artisans 4, Guest Reception 8, Four Directions 2, Gate Office staff 18.

sentences.zh: 是歲十一月，以皇子生，宴集英殿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of that year, because a prince was born, a banquet was held in the Hall of Collected Elegance.
translations.idiomatic: That eleventh month, because a prince was born, a banquet was held in the Hall of Collected Elegance.

sentences.zh: 七年九月，詔：「自今大宴，親王、皇親使相、樞密使副使、宣徽使、駙馬都尉並於殿門外幕次就賜酒食。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the seventh year, an edict: “From now at grand banquets, imperial princes, imperial clansmen with commissioner powers, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner and deputy, Palace Domestic Service commissioner, and imperial sons-in-law shall all receive bestowed wine and food at the tent outside the hall gate.”
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, ninth month: grand-banquet princes, clansmen commissioners, Bureau commissioner and deputy, Palace Domestic Service commissioner, and sons-in-law were to receive wine and food at the tent outside the hall gate.

sentences.zh: 舊制，會食集英西廊之廡下，喧卑為甚，權發遣宣徽院吳充奏其事，故有是命。

translations.literal: The old rule: communal eating under the west wing colonnade of the Hall of Collected Elegance was extremely noisy and low; Acting Palace Domestic Service Commissioner Wu Chong memorialized on this matter, hence this order.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly they ate under the west colonnade of the Hall of Collected Elegance in great noise; Acting Commissioner Wu Chong reported this, hence the order.

sentences.zh: 元豐七年三月，大宴集英殿，命皇子延安郡王侍立。

translations.literal: In the third month of the seventh year of Yuanfeng, a grand banquet was held in the Hall of Collected Elegance; the prince, Prince of Yan’an Commandery, was ordered to attend standing.
translations.idiomatic: the seventh year of Yuanfeng, third month: a grand banquet in the Hall of Collected Elegance; the Prince of Yan’an Commandery stood in attendance.

sentences.zh: 宰相王珪等率百官廷賀。

translations.literal: Chief Counselor Wang Gui and others led the hundred officials in court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Counselor Wang Gui and others led the officials in court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「皇家慶事，與卿等同之。」

translations.literal: Edict: “The imperial house has a celebration, shared with you.”
translations.idiomatic: Edict: “The imperial house celebrates, and shares it with you.”

sentences.zh: 珪等再拜稱謝。

translations.literal: Gui and others bowed again in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Gui and the others bowed again in thanks.

sentences.zh: 久之，王乃退。

translations.literal: After some time, the prince then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After a time the prince withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時王未出閣，帝 特令侍宴，以見群臣。

translations.literal: At that time the prince had not yet left the palace; the emperor specially ordered him to attend the banquet to be seen by the ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The prince had not yet left the palace; the emperor specially had him attend so the ministers could see him.

sentences.zh: 九年，閣門言：「大宴不用兩軍妓女，隻用教坊小兒之舞。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year, the Gate Office said: “Grand banquets do not use the two armies’ female performers; only the Music Office boys’ dances are used.”
translations.idiomatic: Year 9: the Gate Office said grand banquets no longer used the two armies’ female performers, only Music Office boys’ dances.

sentences.zh: 王拱辰請以女童代之。

translations.literal: Wang Gongchen requested that girl performers replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gongchen asked to substitute girl performers.

sentences.zh: 元祐八年，詔罷獨看。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Yuanyou, an edict canceled the solo preview.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 8: an edict canceled the solo preview.

sentences.zh: 故事，大宴前一日，御殿閱百戲， 謂之獨看。

translations.literal: By precedent, on the day before a grand banquet the emperor in the hall reviewed the hundred entertainments, called the solo preview.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent the day before a grand banquet the emperor reviewed entertainments in the hall—the solo preview.

sentences.zh: 修國史范祖禹言：「是日進《神宗紀》草，陛下覽先帝史冊甫畢，即觀百戲，理似未安，故請罷之。」

translations.literal: Fan Zuyu, revising the national history, said: “On that day the draft of the Taizong Annals was submitted; when Your Majesty had just finished reading the former emperor’s annals and then viewed the hundred entertainments, the principle seems not yet settled; therefore I ask to cancel it.”
translations.idiomatic: Historian Fan Zuyu said: “That day the Taizong annals draft was submitted; after reading your father’s annals to view entertainments seems improper—please cancel the preview.”

sentences.zh: 元祐二年九月，經筵講《論語》徹 章，賜宰臣、執政、經筵官宴於東宮，帝親書唐人詩分賜之。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year of Yuanyou, when the classics lecture on the Analects finished a chapter, the chief counselor, administrators, and classics lecturers were banqueted in the Eastern Palace; the emperor personally wrote Tang poems and bestowed them.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanyou 2, ninth month: after a classics lecture on the Analects finished, counselors and lecturers were banqueted in the Eastern Palace and given Tang poems in the emperor’s hand.

sentences.zh: 三年六月，罷春宴。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year, the spring banquet was canceled.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, sixth month: the spring banquet was canceled.

sentences.zh: 八月，罷秋宴，以魏王出殯，翰林學士蘇軾不進教坊致語故也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the autumn banquet was canceled because the Prince of Wei was being escorted in funeral, and because Hanlin Academician Su Shi did not submit the Music Office congratulatory address.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: the autumn banquet was canceled for the Prince of Wei’s funeral and because Su Shi did not submit the Music Office address.

sentences.zh: 是後以時雨未足， 集英殿試舉人，尚書省火，禁中祈禳，邠國公主未菆，皆罷宴。

translations.literal: Thereafter, when seasonal rain was insufficient, when the Hall of Collected Elegance examination for candidates was held, when the Secretariat caught fire, when prayers were offered in the forbidden precinct, and when the Princess of Bin had not yet been buried—all canceled the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter insufficient rain, examinations in the Hall of Collected Elegance, Secretariat fire, forbidden-precinct prayers, and the Princess of Bin’s unburied state all canceled banquets.

sentences.zh: 凡大宴有故而罷，賜賜預宴官酒饌於閣門朝堂，升殿官雖假故不從遊宴，亦遣中使就第賜焉。

translations.literal: Whenever a grand banquet was canceled for cause, wine and food were bestowed on officials who would have attended at the Gate Office audience hall; officials who ascended the hall though on leave and not attending the tour banquet were also sent eunuchs to bestow at their residences.
translations.idiomatic: When a grand banquet was canceled, wine and food were sent to would-be guests at the Gate Office audience hall; even officials on leave who would have ascended received eunuch deliveries at home.

sentences.zh: 親王、 中書、樞密、宣徽、三司使副、學士、步軍都虞候以上、三師、三公、東宮三師三公以下、曾任中書門下致仕者，亦同。

translations.literal: Imperial princes, Secretariat, Bureau of Military Affairs, Palace Domestic Service, Three Departments deputy commissioners, academicians, palace guard commanders and above, the Three Preceptors, Three Excellencies, Eastern Palace Three Preceptors and Three Excellencies and below, and former Secretariat and Chancellery officials retired—all the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same applied to princes, Secretariat, Bureau, Palace Domestic Service, Three Departments deputies, academicians, guard commanders and above, Three Preceptors, Three Excellencies, Eastern Palace preceptors, and retired chief counselors.

sentences.zh: 凡外國使預宴者，祥符中宴崇 德殿，夏使於西廊南赴坐，交使以次歇空，進奉、押衙次交州，契丹舍利、從人則於東廊南赴坐。

translations.literal: For foreign envoys attending banquets: in Xiangfu they banqueted in the Hall of Honored Virtue; Xia envoys sat south in the west wing; Jiaozhi envoys took empty seats in order; tribute and military commissioners followed Jiaozhi; Khitan relics and attendants sat south in the east wing.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign guests at banquets: under Xiangfu in the Hall of Honored Virtue; Xia envoys south in the west wing; Jiaozhi in order; tribute commissioners after Jiaozhi; Khitan relics and attendants south in the east wing.

sentences.zh: 四年，又升甘州、交州於朵殿，夏州押衙於東廊南頭歇空坐。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Ganzhou and Jiaozhi were again raised to the side hall; Xia military commissioners sat at the south head of the east wing in empty seats.
translations.idiomatic: Year 4: Ganzhou and Jiaozhi moved to the side hall; Xia commissioners took empty seats at the south end of the east wing.

sentences.zh: 七 年，龜茲進奉人使歇空坐於契丹舍利之下。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Kucha tribute envoys sat in empty seats below Khitan relics.
translations.idiomatic: Year 7: Kucha envoys sat below Khitan relics.

sentences.zh: 其後又令龜茲使副於西廊南赴坐，進奉、押衙重行於後，瓜州、沙州使、副亦於西廊之南赴坐，其餘大略以是為準。

translations.literal: Later Kucha envoy and deputy were ordered to sit south in the west wing; tribute and military commissioners again in rows behind; Guazhou and Shazhou envoys and deputies also south in the west wing—the rest broadly followed this as standard.
translations.idiomatic: Later Kucha envoy and deputy sat south in the west wing with tribute commissioners behind; Guazhou and Shazhou envoys likewise—the rest followed this pattern.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，議禮局上集英殿春秋大宴儀：

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan, the Ritual Discussion Office submitted the spring and autumn grand banquet protocol for the Hall of Collected Elegance:
translations.idiomatic: Daguan 3: the Ritual Discussion Office submitted spring and autumn grand banquet protocol for the Hall of Collected Elegance:

sentences.zh: 其日，預宴文武百僚詣殿庭，東西相向立。

translations.literal: On that day, civil and military officials attending the banquet went to the hall court and stood facing east and west.
translations.idiomatic: That day attending officials lined in the courtyard facing east and west.

sentences.zh: 皇帝出禦需雲殿，閣門、內侍、管軍等起居。

translations.literal: The emperor emerged to attend at the Hall of Clouds Needed; the Gate Office, inner attendants, and army supervisors paid respects.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor emerged at the Hall of Clouds Needed; Gate Office, attendants, and army supervisors paid respects.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降坐，御集英殿，鳴鞭，殿中監已下通班起居。

translations.literal: The emperor descended and attended at the Hall of Collected Elegance; the whip was sounded; from the hall supervisor down they paid respects in full audience.
translations.idiomatic: He descended to the Hall of Collected Elegance; the whip sounded; from the hall supervisor down all paid respects.

sentences.zh: 殿中監、少監升殿，通喚閣門官升殿。

translations.literal: The hall supervisor and vice supervisor ascended the hall and summoned Gate Office officials to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Hall supervisor and deputy ascended and summoned Gate officials up.

sentences.zh: 攝左右軍巡使靴笏起居訖，係鞋執杖侍立，餘非應奉官分出。

translations.literal: Acting left and right army patrol commissioners paid respects with boots and tablets finished, tied shoes, held staffs and stood in attendance; the rest who were not attending officials withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Acting army patrol commissioners finished respects, tied shoes, held staffs and stood; non-attendants withdrew.

sentences.zh: 次鍾鼓樓節級就位，四拜起居。

translations.literal: Next the Bell and Drum Tower section leaders took position and bowed four times in respect.
translations.idiomatic: Bell and Drum Tower section leaders took position and bowed four times.

sentences.zh: 次舍人通喚訖，分引群官橫行北向，東上閣門官讚大起居，班首出班俯伏，跪，致辭訖，俯伏，興，復位。

translations.literal: When the secretariat drafter had finished summoning, they led the officials in horizontal lines facing north; the Eastern Upper Gate official praised the great audience; the lead of the rank came out, prostrated, knelt, finished the address, prostrated, rose, and returned to place.
translations.idiomatic: After summoning, officials lined north; the Eastern Upper Gate praised great audience; the rank lead prostrated, addressed, and returned.

sentences.zh: 群官再拜舞蹈，又再拜，讚各就坐，再拜，舍人分引升 殿，席前相向立，朵殿、兩廡官立於席後。

translations.literal: The officials bowed twice and danced, bowed twice again; praised each to take seat, bowed again; the drafter led them up the hall, stood facing each other before the mats; side hall and two-wing officials stood behind the mats.
translations.idiomatic: Officials bowed twice, danced, bowed again, took seats; drafters led them up to face each other before mats; side hall and wing officials stood behind.

sentences.zh: 有遼使則舍人引大遼舍利西入大起居，讚各就坐，讚再拜，讚就坐，引升西廊。

translations.literal: If there was a Liao envoy, the drafter led the Great Liao relic west to enter for great audience; praised each to seat, praised bow again, praised take seat, led up the west wing.
translations.idiomatic: With a Liao envoy, the drafter led the Liao relic west for great audience, then to the west wing seats.

sentences.zh: 次舍人傳事引從人分入，四拜起居，謝 坐，並同舍利儀。

translations.literal: Next the drafter led attendants in separately; four bows and respects; thanked for seating—all as the relic protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants entered separately, bowed four times, thanked for seats—same as the relic protocol.

sentences.zh: 教坊使以下通班大起居，看盞人謝，升殿再拜。

translations.literal: From the Music Office commissioner down, full audience great respect; the cup-viewer thanked and ascended the hall to bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: From the Music Office commissioner down came great audience; cup-viewers thanked and bowed twice on the hall.

sentences.zh: 內侍進禦茶床，殿侍酹酒訖，次讚天武門外祗候。

translations.literal: Inner attendants brought the imperial tea table; hall attendants poured libation finished; next praised the Tianwu Gate outer attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought the imperial tea table; hall attendants poured libation; Tianwu Gate outer attendants were praised.

sentences.zh: 東上閣門官詣御坐，奏班首姓名以下進酒。

translations.literal: The Eastern Upper Gate official went to the imperial seat and reported the rank lead’s name and those below presenting wine.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Upper Gate official reported the rank lead presenting wine.

sentences.zh: 舍人分引殿上臣僚橫行北向，讚再拜。

translations.literal: The drafter led hall officials in horizontal lines facing north; praised bow again.
translations.idiomatic: Drafters led hall officials north; praised bow again.

sentences.zh: 舍人引班首稍前，東上閣門官接引詣御坐，東北向，搢笏，殿中監奉盤盞授班首，少監啟盞，以酒注之。

translations.literal: The drafter led the rank lead slightly forward; the Eastern Upper Gate official received and led to the imperial seat, northeast facing, inserted tablet; the hall supervisor presented tray and goblet to the rank lead; the vice supervisor opened the goblet and poured wine.
translations.idiomatic: The rank lead advanced; Gate officials led him northeast, inserted tablet; hall supervisor presented tray; vice supervisor poured.

sentences.zh: 班首奉詣御前進 訖，少退，虛跪，興，以槃授殿中監，出笏，東上閣門官引退，舍人接引復位，讚再拜。

translations.literal: The rank lead presented and went before the emperor finished; slightly withdrew, knelt in empty seat, rose, gave tray to hall supervisor, withdrew tablet; the Eastern Upper Gate official led withdrawal; the drafter led back to place; praised bow again.
translations.idiomatic: The rank lead presented wine, knelt, rose, returned tray, withdrew; Gate officials led back; praised bow again.

sentences.zh: 舍人引班首稍前，殿上臣僚席前相向立，東上閣門官接引詣御坐，東北向， 搢笏，殿中監授槃，奉詣御前，西向立，樂作，皇帝飲訖。

translations.literal: The drafter led the rank lead slightly forward; hall officials stood facing each other before mats; the Eastern Upper Gate official received and led to the imperial seat, northeast facing, inserted tablet; the hall supervisor presented tray, went before the emperor, stood west facing; music played; the emperor finished drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Again the rank lead advanced; officials faced each other; he presented at the imperial seat while music played until the emperor drank.

sentences.zh: 舍人分引殿上臣僚橫行北向，東上閣門引班首接盞，退，虛跪，興，授盞殿中監，出笏，引退，舍人接引 復位，讚再拜，讚各賜酒，群臣再拜，讚各就坐，群官皆立席後，復讚就坐。

translations.literal: The drafter led hall officials in horizontal lines facing north; the Eastern Upper Gate led the rank lead to receive the goblet, withdraw, knelt in empty seat, rose, gave goblet to hall supervisor, withdrew tablet, led withdrawal; the drafter led back to place; praised bow again; praised each bestowed wine; the ministers bowed again; praised each to take seat; all officials stood behind mats; again praised to take seat.
translations.idiomatic: Officials lined north; the rank lead received the goblet, withdrew, bowed, took seat; all were praised to seats behind their mats.

sentences.zh: 酒初行，群官搢笏受酒，先宰相，次百官，皆作樂。

translations.literal: At the first round of wine, officials inserted tablets and received wine; first the chief counselor, then the hundred officials—all with music.
translations.idiomatic: First wine round: officials inserted tablets and received wine—chief counselor first, then all—with music.

sentences.zh: 皇帝再舉酒，

translations.literal: The emperor raised wine a second time,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raised wine a second time,

sentences.zh: 〈（並殿 中監、少監進。）〉

translations.literal: (Both hall supervisor and vice supervisor advanced.)
translations.idiomatic: (Hall supervisor and deputy both advanced.)

sentences.zh: 群臣俱立席後，樂作，飲訖，讚各就坐。

translations.literal: The ministers all stood behind their mats; music played; when drinking was finished, praised each to take seat.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers stood behind mats; music played; when finished, praised to seats.

sentences.zh: 復行群臣酒，飲訖。

translations.literal: Again the ministers’ wine was served; when drinking was finished.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers’ wine was served again until finished.

sentences.zh: 皇帝三舉酒，皆如第一之儀。

translations.literal: The emperor raised wine a third time, all as in the first protocol.
translations.idiomatic: The third imperial round followed the first protocol.

sentences.zh: 尚食典奉御進食，太官設群臣食，樂作。

translations.literal: The Imperial Food Office director advanced food; the Grand Steward set food for the ministers; music played.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food director advanced food; Grand Steward set ministers’ food; music played.

sentences.zh: 賜祗應臣僚酒 食，讚謝拜訖，復位。

translations.literal: Bestowed wine and food on attendant officials; praised thanks and bow finished; returned to place.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant officials received wine and food, thanked, bowed, and returned.

sentences.zh: 皇帝四舉酒，

translations.literal: The emperor raised wine a fourth time,
translations.idiomatic: The emperor raised wine a fourth time,

sentences.zh: 〈（並典禦進酒。）〉

translations.literal: (Both Imperial Kitchen attendants advanced wine.)
translations.idiomatic: (Imperial Kitchen attendants advanced wine.)

sentences.zh: 樂工致語，群官皆立席後，致語訖，讚百官再拜，就坐，樂作。

translations.literal: The musicians delivered an address; all officials stood behind their mats; when the address was finished, praised the hundred officials to bow again, take seat; music played.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians addressed; officials stood behind mats; after the address all bowed, sat; music played.

sentences.zh: 皇帝五舉酒，樂工奏樂，庭下舞隊致詞，樂 作，舞隊出。

translations.literal: The emperor raised wine a fifth time; musicians played; the courtyard dance troupe delivered words; music played; the dance troupe withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth imperial round: musicians played; courtyard dancers addressed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 東上閣門奏再坐時刻。

translations.literal: The Eastern Upper Gate reported the time for second seating.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Upper Gate reported time for second seating.

sentences.zh: 俟放隊訖，內侍舉禦茶床，皇帝降坐，鳴鞭，群臣退。

translations.literal: When the troupe was dismissed finished, inner attendants raised the imperial tea table; the emperor descended, the whip sounded; the ministers withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After the troupe left, attendants raised the tea table; the emperor descended; ministers withdrew.

sentences.zh: 賜花，再坐。

translations.literal: Flowers were bestowed; second seating.
translations.idiomatic: Flowers were bestowed; second seating began.

sentences.zh: 前二刻，御史臺、東上閣門催班，群官戴花北 向立，內侍進班齊牌，皇帝詣集英殿，百官謝花再拜，又再拜就坐。

translations.literal: Two quarters before, the Censorate and Eastern Upper Gate urged the ranks; officials wore flowers and stood facing north; inner attendants advanced the ranks with tablets aligned; the emperor went to the Hall of Collected Elegance; the hundred officials thanked for flowers with two bows, bowed twice again and took seat.
translations.idiomatic: Two quarters earlier the Censorate and Gate urged ranks; officials wore flowers facing north; the emperor entered the Hall of Collected Elegance; all thanked for flowers with two bows and sat.

sentences.zh: 內侍進禦茶床，皇帝舉酒，殿上奏樂，庭下作樂。

translations.literal: Inner attendants brought the imperial tea table; the emperor raised wine; music played on the hall; music played in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants brought the tea table; the emperor raised wine with hall and courtyard music.

sentences.zh: 皇帝再舉酒，殿上奏樂，庭下舞隊前致語，樂 作，出。

translations.literal: The emperor raised wine a second time; music on the hall; the courtyard dance troupe addressed in front; music played; withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Second round: hall music; courtyard dancers addressed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 皇帝三舉酒、四舉酒皆如上儀。

translations.literal: The emperor’s third and fourth rounds of wine all followed the above protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Third and fourth rounds followed the same protocol.

sentences.zh: 若宣示盞，即隨所向，閣門官以下揖稱宣示盞，躬讚就坐。

translations.literal: If an edict cup was proclaimed, then according to direction; Gate Office officials and below bowed and called “proclaimed cup,” bowed and praised to take seat.
translations.idiomatic: If a proclaimed cup was issued, Gate officials bowed, announced it, and praised all to seat.

sentences.zh: 若宣勸，即立席後躬飲訖，讚再拜。

translations.literal: If encouragement was proclaimed, they stood behind the mat, bowed and drank finished, praised bow again.
translations.idiomatic: If encouragement was proclaimed, they stood behind the mat, drank, and bowed again.

sentences.zh: 內侍舉禦茶床，舍人引班首 以下降階再拜舞蹈，又再拜訖，分班出。

translations.literal: Inner attendants raised the imperial tea table; the drafter led the rank lead and those below down the steps to bow twice and dance, bow twice again finished, divided ranks and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants raised the tea table; drafters led officials down to bow twice, dance, bow again, and exit by ranks.

sentences.zh: 閣門官側奏無公事，皇帝降坐，鳴鞭。

translations.literal: The Gate Office official reported at the side that there was no official business; the emperor descended and the whip sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Gate officials reported no business; the emperor descended and the whip sounded.

sentences.zh: 集英殿飲福大宴儀。

translations.literal: Hall of Collected Elegance Drinking the Blessing grand banquet protocol.
translations.idiomatic: Hall of Collected Elegance Drinking the Blessing grand banquet protocol.

sentences.zh: 初，大禮畢，皇帝逐頓飲福，餘酒封進入內。

translations.literal: At first, when the great rite was completed, the emperor at each stage drank the blessing; remaining wine was sealed and sent into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: After great rites the emperor drank the blessing at each stage; leftover wine was sealed and sent within.

sentences.zh: 宴日降出，酒既三行，泛賜預坐臣僚飲福酒各一盞，群臣飲訖，宣勸，各興，立席後，讚再拜謝訖，復坐飲，並如春秋大宴之儀。

translations.literal: On banquet day it was sent down; when wine had gone three rounds, blessing wine one goblet each was broadly bestowed on seated ministers; when the ministers had drunk finished, encouragement was proclaimed; each rose, stood behind the mat, praised bow in thanks finished, sat again and drank—all as in the spring and autumn grand banquet protocol.
translations.idiomatic: On banquet day, after three rounds each seated minister received one goblet of blessing wine; after drinking, encouragement was proclaimed; all rose, bowed behind the mat, and sat again—as in spring and autumn grand banquets.

sentences.zh: 紹興十三年三月三日，詔宴殿陳設止用緋、黃二色，不用文繡，令有司遵守，更不製造。

translations.literal: On the third day of the third month of the thirteenth year of Shaoxing, an edict: banquet hall furnishings use only crimson and yellow, not patterned brocade; order the relevant offices to observe and make no more.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxing 13, third month, day 3: banquet furnishings were limited to crimson and yellow without brocade patterns, and no new ones were to be made.

sentences.zh: 五月，閣門修立集英殿大宴儀注。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Gate Office revised and established the grand banquet regulations for the Hall of Collected Elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: the Gate Office revised grand banquet regulations for the Hall of Collected Elegance.

sentences.zh: 乾道八月十二月，詔今後前宰相到闕，如遇赴宴賜茶，其合會墩杌，非特旨，並依官品。

translations.literal: In the eighth and twelfth months of the Qiandao era, an edict: hereafter when a former chief counselor arrives at court, if he attends a banquet or bestowed tea, the combined meeting cushions and stools, unless by special edict, all follow official rank.
translations.idiomatic: Qiandao 8–12: former chief counselors attending banquets or bestowed tea used cushions and stools by rank unless specially ordered.

sentences.zh: 又行門、禁衛諸色祗應人，依紹興例，並賜絹花。

translations.literal: Also for Gate Office, guard, and all colored attendant personnel, following the Shaoxing precedent, silk flowers were all bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Gate, guard, and attendant personnel also received silk flowers per the Shaoxing precedent.

sentences.zh: 自是惟正旦、生辰、郊祀及金使見辭各有宴，然大宴視東京時則亦簡矣。

translations.literal: From this only New Year’s Day, birthday, suburban sacrifice, and Jin envoy farewell audiences each had banquets, but grand banquets compared with the Eastern Capital period were also simpler.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth only New Year, birthday, suburban sacrifice, and Jin envoy farewells had banquets, and even grand banquets were simpler than at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 曲宴。

translations.literal: Informal banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Informal banquet.

sentences.zh: 凡幸苑囿、池禦，觀稼、畋獵，所至設宴，惟從官預，謂之曲宴。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor visited gardens, imperial pools, viewed the harvest, or hunted, wherever he arrived a banquet was set; only attending officials participated—called an informal banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor visited gardens, pools, viewed crops, or hunted, attending officials alone were feasted—an informal banquet.

sentences.zh: 或宴大遼使、副於紫宸殿，則近臣及刺史、正郎、都虞候以上預。

translations.literal: Or when entertaining the Great Liao envoy and deputy in the Hall of Purple Felicity, then close ministers and those from prefect, regular director, and commandant rank up participated.
translations.idiomatic: Entertaining Great Liao envoys in the Hall of Purple Felicity included close ministers and officials from prefect, director, and commandant upward.

sentences.zh: 暮春後苑賞花、釣魚，則三館、秘閣皆預。

translations.literal: In late spring, flower viewing and fishing in the rear garden, then the Three Institutes and Secret Repository all participated.
translations.idiomatic: Late-spring flower viewing and fishing in the rear garden included the Three Institutes and Secret Repository.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆元年七月，親征澤、潞，宴從臣於河陽行宮，又宴韓令坤已下於禮賢講武殿，賜襲衣、器幣、鞍馬，以賞澤、潞之功也。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Jianlong, the emperor personally campaigned against Ze and Lu, banqueted attending ministers at the Heyang traveling palace, and again banqueted Han Lingkun and those below at the Hall of Honoring the Worthy and Martial Lectures, bestowing robes, vessels, coins, saddles, and horses to reward the Ze and Lu achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Jianlong 1, seventh month: campaigning against Ze and Lu, the emperor banqueted ministers at Heyang and again at the Hall of Honoring Worthies, rewarding the Ze-Lu campaign with robes, vessels, and horses.

sentences.zh: 四年四月，宴從臣於玉津園。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year, he banqueted attending ministers at the Jade Ford Garden.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, fourth month: he banqueted ministers at the Jade Ford Garden.

sentences.zh: 乾 德三年七月六日，詔皇弟開封尹、宰相、樞密使、翰林學士、中書舍人泛舟後苑新池，張樂宴飲，極歡而罷。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the seventh month of the third year of Qiande, an edict: the imperial younger brother, chief counselor, Bureau commissioner, Hanlin academicians, and secretariat drafters floated on the rear garden’s new pool; music was played and they drank, ending in utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: Qiande 3, seventh month, day 6: the imperial brother, chief counselor, Bureau commissioner, Hanlin scholars, and drafters boated on the new rear-garden pool with music until joyful exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 是歲重陽，宴近臣於長春殿。

translations.literal: That year on Double Yang, he banqueted close ministers at the Hall of Everlasting Spring.
translations.idiomatic: That Double Yang he banqueted close ministers in the Hall of Everlasting Spring.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興 國九年三月十五日，詔宰相、近臣賞花於後苑，帝曰：「春氣暄和，萬物暢茂，四方無事。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of the third month of the ninth year of Taiping Xingguo, an edict: chief counselor and close ministers view flowers in the rear garden; the emperor said: “Spring air is warm and harmonious; the ten thousand things flourish; the four quarters are without affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 9, third month, day 15: close ministers were summoned to view rear-garden flowers; the emperor said: “Spring is mild, all things flourish, and the realm is at peace.

sentences.zh: 朕以天下之樂為樂，宜令侍從詞臣各賦詩。」

translations.literal: I take the realm’s joy as my joy; it is fitting to order attending literary officials each to compose a poem.”
translations.idiomatic: I take the realm’s joy as my own; let each attending literary official compose a poem.”

sentences.zh: 帝習射於水心殿。

translations.literal: The emperor practiced archery at the Water Heart Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor practiced archery at the Water Heart Hall.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年 四月二日，詔輔臣、三司使、翰林、樞密直學士、尚書省四品兩省五品以上、三館學士宴於後苑，賞花、釣魚，張樂賜飲，命群臣賦詩習射。

translations.literal: On the second day of the fourth month of the second year of Yongxi, an edict: assisting ministers, Three Departments commissioner, Hanlin and Bureau direct academicians, Secretariat and Chancellery fourth rank and fifth rank and above, and Three Institutes academicians banquet in the rear garden, viewing flowers and fishing; music was played and drink bestowed; he ordered the ministers to compose poems and practice archery.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi 2, fourth month, day 2: ministers, Three Departments commissioner, Hanlin and Bureau scholars, high Secretariat and Chancellery officials, and Three Institutes scholars banqueted in the rear garden for flowers, fishing, poetry, and archery.

sentences.zh: 賞花曲宴自此始。

translations.literal: Flower-viewing informal banquets began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Flower-viewing informal banquets began here.

sentences.zh: 三年 十二月一日，大雨雪，帝喜，禦玉華殿，召宰臣及近臣謂曰：「春夏以來，未嘗飲酒，今得此嘉雪，思與卿等同醉。」

translations.literal: On the first day of the twelfth month of the third year, great snow fell; the emperor was pleased and attended the Jade Splendor Hall, summoned chief counselor and close ministers and said: “Since spring and summer I have not drunk wine; now with this fine snow I wish to get drunk together with you.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, twelfth month, day 1: heavy snow pleased the emperor; at the Jade Splendor Hall he told counselors: “Since spring I have not drunk; with this snow I wish to drink with you.

sentences.zh: 又出御製《雪詩》，令侍臣屬和。

translations.literal: He also produced an imperial “Snow Poem” and ordered the attending officials to compose matching pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote an imperial Snow Poem and ordered matching verses.

sentences.zh: 後凡曲宴不 盡載。

translations.literal: Later informal banquets are not all recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Later informal banquets are not all recorded.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平元年二月二十二日，宴群臣於崇德殿，不作樂。

translations.literal: On the twenty-second day of the second month of the first year of Xianping of Zhenzong, he banqueted the ministers in the Hall of Honored Virtue without music.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong, Xianping 1, second month, day 22: ministers were banqueted in the Hall of Honored Virtue without music.

sentences.zh: 二年八月七日，再宴，用樂。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the eighth month of the second year, he banqueted again, with music.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, eighth month, day 7: another banquet, with music.

sentences.zh: 三年二月晦，賞花，宴於後苑，帝作《中春賞花釣魚 詩》，儒臣皆賦，遂射於水殿，盡歡而罷。

translations.literal: On the last day of the second month of the third year, viewing flowers, he banqueted in the rear garden; the emperor composed “Mid-Spring Flower Viewing and Fishing Poem”; Confucian officials all composed; then they shot at the Water Hall and ended in full joy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, second month, last day: flower viewing in the rear garden with an imperial poem; scholars composed; archery at the Water Hall ended the day.

sentences.zh: 自是遂為定制。

translations.literal: From this it became a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: This became fixed practice.

sentences.zh: 四年十一月二十日，禦龍圖閣曲宴，詔近臣觀太宗草、行、飛白、篆、籀、八分書及畫。

translations.literal: On the twentieth day of the eleventh month of the fourth year, an informal banquet at the Dragon Diagram Hall; close ministers were ordered to view Taizong’s draft, running, flying-white, seal, large-seal, and eight-divisions scripts and paintings.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, eleventh month, day 20: informal banquet at the Dragon Diagram Hall; close ministers viewed Taizong’s calligraphy and paintings.

sentences.zh: 景德二年十二月 五日，宴尚書省五品、諸軍都指揮使以上、契丹使於崇德殿，不舉樂，以明德太后喪製故也。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the twelfth month of the second year of Jingde, he banqueted Secretariat fifth rank, various army commanders and above, and Khitan envoys in the Hall of Honored Virtue without music, because of mourning regulations for Empress Mingde.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde 2, twelfth month, day 5: fifth-rank Secretariat officials, army commanders, and Khitan envoys were banqueted without music for Empress Mingde’s mourning.

sentences.zh: 時契丹初來賀承天節，擇膳夫五人齎本國異味，就尚食局造食，詔賜膳 夫衣服、銀帶、器帛。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan had first come to congratulate the Ascension Day; five cooks were chosen to bring their state’s exotic flavors to the Imperial Kitchen to prepare food; an edict bestowed the cooks clothes, silver belts, vessels, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan envoys had first come for Ascension Day; five cooks prepared their native dishes in the Imperial Kitchen and received clothes, belts, and silks.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符六年七月二十九日，詔輔臣觀粟於後苑禦山子，觀御製文閣御書及《嘉禾圖》，賜飲。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month of the sixth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict: assisting ministers view grain at the rear garden imperial mountain pavilion, view imperial compositions in the Literary Hall and the “Fine Grain Picture,” and were bestowed drink.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong Xiangfu 6, seventh month, day 29: ministers viewed grain at the rear-garden mountain pavilion, viewed imperial writings and the Fine Grain Picture, and were given drink.

sentences.zh: 是日，皇子從遊。

translations.literal: That day the prince accompanied the tour.
translations.idiomatic: That day the prince joined the tour.

sentences.zh: 天禧四年七月十一日，詔近 臣及寇準、馮拯觀內苑穀，遂宴於玉宸殿。

translations.literal: On the eleventh day of the seventh month of the fourth year of Tianxi, an edict: close ministers and Kou Zhun and Feng Zhen view inner-garden grain; then banquet at the Jade Felicity Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi 4, seventh month, day 11: close ministers, Kou Zhun, and Feng Zhen viewed inner-garden grain and banqueted at the Jade Felicity Hall.

sentences.zh: 十月二十九日，詔皇太子、宗室、近臣、諸帥赴玉宸殿翠芳亭觀稻，賜宴，仍以稻分賜之。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the tenth month, an edict: the crown prince, imperial clan, close ministers, and various commanders went to the Emerald Fragrance Pavilion of the Jade Felicity Hall to view rice; banquet was bestowed, and rice was also distributed to them.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, day 29: the crown prince, clan, close ministers, and commanders viewed rice at the Emerald Fragrance Pavilion and received banquet and rice.

sentences.zh: 仁宗天聖二年， 既禫除，百官五表請聽樂，而秋燕用樂之半。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiansheng of Renzong, after the end of mourning, the hundred officials five times memorialized to request music; the autumn banquet used half music.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong, Tiansheng 2: after mourning ended officials repeatedly asked for music; the autumn banquet used half music.

sentences.zh: 詔輔臣曰：「昨日宴宮中，朕數四上勉皇太后聽樂。」

translations.literal: An edict to assisting ministers: “Yesterday at the inner palace banquet I several times urged the empress dowager to listen to music.”
translations.idiomatic: He told ministers: “Yesterday at the inner banquet I repeatedly urged the empress dowager to hear music.”

sentences.zh: 王欽若以聞太后，太后曰：「自先帝棄天下，吾終身不欲聽樂。

translations.literal: Wang Qinruo reported this to the empress dowager; the empress dowager said: “Since the former emperor abandoned the realm, I have all my life not wished to hear music.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qinruo told the empress dowager, who said: “Since the late emperor’s death I have never wished to hear music.

sentences.zh: 皇帝再三為請，其可重違乎！」

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly requested—how can I heavily violate this!”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again and again—how can I refuse so firmly!”

sentences.zh: 明年上元節，乃朝謁景靈上清宮、啟聖院、相國寺，還禦正陽門，宴從官，觀燈。

translations.literal: The next year on the Upper Yuan festival, he then paid court at the Jingling Upper Pure Palace, Qisheng Courtyard, and Xiangguo Temple, returned and attended at the Proper Yang Gate, banqueted attending officials, and viewed lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: Next Upper Yuan he worshiped at Jingling, Qisheng, and Xiangguo, returned to the Proper Yang Gate, banqueted attendants, and viewed lanterns.

sentences.zh: 次日，太后召命婦臨觀。

translations.literal: The next day the empress dowager summoned titled women to attend and view.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the empress dowager summoned titled women to view.

sentences.zh: 及春秋大宴，歲為常。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn grand banquets became annual.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn grand banquets became annual events.

sentences.zh: 夏，觀南禦莊刈麥，秋，瑞聖園刈穀，並宴從官，或射，不為常。

translations.literal: In summer, viewing wheat harvest at the Southern Imperial Estate; in autumn, harvesting grain at the Auspicious Sage Garden—both banqueted attending officials, sometimes with archery—not fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Summer wheat viewing at the Southern Imperial Estate and autumn harvest at the Auspicious Sage Garden included attendant banquets and sometimes archery, but not on a fixed schedule.

sentences.zh: 皇祐五年，後苑寶政殿刈麥，謂輔臣曰：「朕新作此殿，不欲植花，歲以種麥，庶知穡事不易也。」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Huangyou, harvesting wheat at the Baozheng Hall in the rear garden, he told assisting ministers: “I newly built this hall and did not wish to plant flowers; each year I plant wheat so I may know how hard farming is.”
translations.idiomatic: Huangyou 5: harvesting wheat at Baozheng Hall, he told ministers: “I built this hall for wheat, not flowers, to remember how hard farming is.”

sentences.zh: 自是幸觀穀、麥，惟就後苑，春夏賞花、釣魚則歲為之。

translations.literal: From this, viewing grain and wheat was only in the rear garden; spring and summer flower viewing and fishing were annual.
translations.idiomatic: Grain viewing stayed in the rear garden; spring and summer flowers and fishing were annual.

sentences.zh: 嘉祐七上十二月，特召兩府、近臣、三司副使、台諫官、皇子、宗室、駙馬都尉，管軍臣僚至龍圖、天章 閣，觀三聖御書，及寶文閣為飛白分賜，下逮館閣官，製《觀書詩》，賜韓琦以下和進，遂宴群玉殿，傳詔學士王珪撰詩序，刊石於閣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the seventh year of Jiayou, he specially summoned the two administrations, close ministers, Three Departments deputy commissioners, censorial and remonstrance officials, princes, imperial clan, imperial sons-in-law, and army supervisors to the Dragon Diagram and Heavenly Chapter halls to view the three emperors’ imperial writings; the Baowen Hall produced flying-white to distribute down to pavilion officials; he composed “Viewing Books Poem” and bestowed it to Han Qi and those below to match and submit; then banqueted at the Hall of Gathered Jade; he transmitted an edict for Academician Wang Gui to compose a preface and carve it on stone in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Jiayou 7, twelfth month: two administrations, close ministers, censors, princes, clan, sons-in-law, and army leaders viewed imperial writings at Dragon Diagram and Heavenly Chapter; flying-white was distributed; a banquet at Gathered Jade followed with a stone preface by Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 數日，再會天章閣，觀三朝 瑞物，復宴群玉殿，酒行，上曰：「天下久無事，今日之樂，與卿等共之，宜盡醉，勿復辭。」

translations.literal: Several days later, again meeting at the Heavenly Chapter Hall to view the three reigns’ auspicious objects, again banquet at the Hall of Gathered Jade; as wine was served the emperor said: “The realm has long been without affairs; today’s joy I share with you—drink fully and do not decline.”
translations.idiomatic: Days later they met again at Heavenly Chapter to view auspicious objects and banqueted at Gathered Jade; the emperor said: “The realm has been at peace long—drink fully with me.”

sentences.zh: 因召韓琦至禦榻前，別賜一大卮。

translations.literal: He then summoned Han Qi before the imperial couch and separately bestowed a large goblet.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Han Qi to the couch and gave him a large goblet apart from the rest.

sentences.zh: 出禁中名花，金盤貯香藥，令各持 歸，莫不沾醉，至暮而罷。

translations.literal: He produced forbidden-palace famous flowers; gold trays stored fragrant medicines; he ordered each to carry them home; none were not thoroughly drunk, ending at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Famous palace flowers and gold trays of fragrance were sent home with each guest; all were thoroughly drunk by dusk.

sentences.zh: 政和二年三月，上巳御筵，詔令移用他日，以國有故，宰臣請罷宴故也。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Zhenghe, the Upper Si imperial feast: an edict moved it to another day because of national mourning; the chief counselors requested canceling the banquet for that reason.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe 2, third month: the Upper Si feast was moved because of national mourning at counselors’ request.

sentences.zh: 大觀三年，議禮局上垂拱殿曲宴儀：

translations.literal: In the third year of Daguan, the Ritual Discussion Office submitted informal banquet protocol for the Hall of Bowed Reverence:
translations.idiomatic: Daguan 3: the Ritual Discussion Office submitted informal banquet protocol for the Hall of Bowed Reverence:

sentences.zh: 皇帝視事畢，東上閣門進呈坐圖，舍人奏閣門無公事，皇帝降坐，鳴鞭，入殿後閣。

translations.literal: When the emperor finished attending to affairs, the Eastern Upper Gate presented the seating chart; the secretariat drafter reported no Gate Office business; the emperor descended and entered the rear hall passage.
translations.idiomatic: After affairs the Eastern Upper Gate presented the seating chart; with no Gate business the emperor entered the rear passage.

sentences.zh: 諸司排設備，東上閣門附內侍奏班齊，皇帝出閣升坐，鳴鞭。

translations.literal: The various offices arranged equipment; the Eastern Upper Gate attached inner attendants reporting ranks aligned; the emperor came out, ascended, and sat; the whip sounded.
translations.idiomatic: Offices arranged equipment; attendants reported aligned ranks; the emperor ascended and the whip sounded.

sentences.zh: 三公、直學士以上、親王、使相至觀察使以上，分東西入，詣殿庭，橫行北向立定。

translations.literal: The Three Excellencies, direct academicians and above, imperial princes, commissioners with ministerial powers to observation commissioners and above, entered divided east and west, went to the hall court, walked horizontally and stood north facing.
translations.idiomatic: Three Excellencies, direct academicians, princes, and commissioners to observation rank entered east and west, lined north in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 班首奏聖躬萬 福，舍人讚各就坐，再拜訖，分引詣東西階升殿，席前相向立。

translations.literal: The rank lead reported “Ten thousand blessings to the Sacred Person”; the drafter praised each to take seat; when bowing was finished, they were led by east and west steps up the hall and stood facing each other before the mats.
translations.idiomatic: The rank lead wished the emperor ten thousand blessings; drafters led all to seats facing each other before the mats.

sentences.zh: 次教坊使以下常起居，次看盞人謝，升殿，次內侍進禦茶床，殿侍酹酒訖，閣門詣御坐，躬奏班首姓 名以下進酒。

translations.literal: Next the Music Office commissioner and below paid regular respects; next the cup-viewer thanked and ascended; next inner attendants brought the imperial tea table; hall attendants poured libation finished; the Gate Office went to the imperial seat, bowed and reported the rank lead’s name and those below presenting wine.
translations.idiomatic: Music Office officials paid respects; cup-viewers thanked and ascended; tea was brought and libation poured; Gate officials reported wine presentation.

sentences.zh: 舍人分引殿上臣僚，橫行北向，讚再拜。

translations.literal: The drafter led hall officials in horizontal lines facing north; praised bow again.
translations.idiomatic: Drafters led hall officials north; praised bow again.

sentences.zh: 班首奉酒躬進，樂作，皇帝飲訖。

translations.literal: The rank lead presented wine with bow; music played; the emperor finished drinking.
translations.idiomatic: The rank lead presented wine; music played until the emperor drank.

sentences.zh: 舍人讚各賜酒，群官俱再拜。

translations.literal: The drafter praised each bestowed wine; all officials together bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: Drafters praised bestowed wine; all bowed again.

sentences.zh: 讚各就坐，群官皆立席後，復讚就坐。

translations.literal: Praised each to take seat; all officials stood behind mats; again praised to take seat.
translations.idiomatic: All were praised to seat, stood behind mats, then praised to seat again.

sentences.zh: 酒初行，先宰相，次百官，皆作樂。

translations.literal: At the first round of wine, first the chief counselor, then the hundred officials—all with music.
translations.idiomatic: First wine round: chief counselor, then all officials, with music.

translations.literal: (Later follow this.)
translations.idiomatic: (Later follow this.)

sentences.zh: 尚食興，奉御進食，太官令設群官食。

translations.literal: The Imperial Food Office rose; the director advanced food; the Grand Steward set officials’ food.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Food rose; director advanced food; Grand Steward set officials’ food.

sentences.zh: 酒五行，若宣示盞，即隨所向，閣門揖稱宣示盞，躬，讚就坐。

translations.literal: Five rounds of wine; if a proclaimed cup, then according to direction; the Gate Office bowed and called “proclaimed cup,” bowed and praised to take seat.
translations.idiomatic: Five wine rounds; proclaimed cups were announced by Gate officials and all praised to seat.

sentences.zh: 若宣勸，即立席後躬飲，讚再拜。

translations.literal: If encouragement was proclaimed, they stood behind the mat, bowed and drank; praised bow again.
translations.idiomatic: Encouragement meant standing behind the mat to drink and bow again.

sentences.zh: 內侍舉禦茶床，舍人引班首以下降階橫行，北向再拜，分班出。

translations.literal: Inner attendants raised the imperial tea table; the drafter led the rank lead and those below down the steps in horizontal lines, bowed north, divided ranks and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants raised the tea table; drafters led officials down, bowed north, and exited by ranks.

sentences.zh: 皇帝降坐。

translations.literal: The emperor descended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor descended.

sentences.zh: 上巳、重陽賜宴儀：

translations.literal: Upper Si and Double Yang bestowed banquet protocol:
translations.idiomatic: Upper Si and Double Yang bestowed banquet protocol:

sentences.zh: 其日，預宴官以下並赴宴所就次，諸司排設備，預宴官以下詣庭中望闕位立。

translations.literal: On that day, officials attending the banquet and below all went to the banquet place and took their places; the various offices arranged equipment; officials attending and below went to the court facing the imperial presence and stood.
translations.idiomatic: That day guests took places after offices arranged equipment and lined facing the imperial presence.

sentences.zh: 次中使詣班首之左，稍前立，中使宣曰「有敕」，在位官皆再拜訖。

translations.literal: Next a eunuch went to the left of the rank lead, stood slightly forward, and proclaimed: “There is an edict”; all present officials bowed again finished.
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch proclaimed “There is an edict”; all bowed.

sentences.zh: 中使宣曰「賜卿等御筵」，在位官皆再拜，搢笏舞蹈，又再拜。

translations.literal: The eunuch proclaimed: “Bestowed to you is an imperial feast”; all present officials bowed again, inserted tablets, danced, and bowed again.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch proclaimed an imperial feast; all bowed, inserted tablets, danced, and bowed again.

sentences.zh: 中使退，預宴官分東西升階就坐。

translations.literal: The eunuch withdrew; attending officials divided east and west, ascended the steps, and took seat.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch withdrew; guests ascended east and west and sat.

sentences.zh: 酒行，樂作。

translations.literal: As wine was served, music played.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was served with music.

sentences.zh: 食訖、食畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When eating was finished and the meal completed, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When food was finished, music stopped.

sentences.zh: 酒五行，預宴官並興就次，賜花有差。

translations.literal: Five rounds of wine; attending officials all rose to their places; flowers were bestowed by rank.
translations.idiomatic: After five rounds guests rose; flowers were bestowed by rank.

sentences.zh: 少頃，戴花畢，與宴官詣望闕位立，謝花，再拜訖，復升就坐。

translations.literal: After a short while, when wearing flowers was finished, banquet officials went to face the imperial presence, thanked for flowers, bowed again finished, ascended again and took seat.
translations.idiomatic: After donning flowers they thanked toward the throne, bowed twice, and sat again.

sentences.zh: 酒行，樂作。

translations.literal: Wine was served; music played.
translations.idiomatic: Wine was served again with music.

sentences.zh: 飲訖、食畢，樂止。

translations.literal: When drinking and the meal were finished, music stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When drinking and food ended, music stopped.
