sentences.zh: 酒四行而退。

translations.literal: Four rounds of wine and withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Four more rounds and the banquet ended.

sentences.zh: 遊觀。

translations.literal: Outings.
translations.idiomatic: Outings.

sentences.zh: 天子歲時遊豫，則上元幸集禧觀、相國寺，禦宣德門觀燈；

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven at the seasons went out for pleasure, then at the Upper Yuan he visited the Jixi Temple and Xiangguo Temple and attended at the Xuande Gate to view lanterns;
translations.idiomatic: Seasonal imperial outings included Upper Yuan visits to Jixi and Xiangguo temples and lantern viewing at Xuande Gate;

sentences.zh: 首夏幸金明池觀水嬉，瓊林苑宴射；

translations.literal: at the start of summer he visited the Golden Bright Pond to view water games, and at the Jade Forest Garden banqueted and shot;
translations.idiomatic: early summer brought the Golden Bright Pond for water games and the Jade Forest Garden for banquets and archery;

sentences.zh: 大祀禮成，則幸太一宮、集禧觀、相國寺恭謝，或詣諸寺觀焚香，或至近郊閱武、觀稼，其事蓋不一焉。

translations.literal: when great sacrifice rites were completed, he visited the Great Unity Temple, Jixi Temple, and Xiangguo Temple to offer thanks, or went to various temples and abbeys to burn incense, or to the near suburbs to review troops or view the harvest—the matters were not one kind.
translations.idiomatic: after great sacrifices he thanked at Great Unity, Jixi, and Xiangguo, burned incense at temples, or reviewed troops and crops nearby—the occasions varied widely.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆元年四月，幸玉津園。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Jianlong of Taizu, he visited the Jade Ford Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, Jianlong 1, fourth month: Jade Ford Garden.

sentences.zh: 是後凡十三臨幸。

translations.literal: Thereafter he visited thirteen times in all.
translations.idiomatic: He visited thirteen times thereafter.

sentences.zh: 九月，幸宜春苑。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he visited the Spring Delight Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Spring Delight Garden.

sentences.zh: 是後觀習水戰者二十有八，幸大相國寺、封禪寺者各五，龍興寺及皇弟開封尹園各三，幸太清 觀、建隆觀者再，崇夏寺、廣化寺、等覺寺者各一，觀水磑者八，閱炮車、觀水櫃、觀稼、幸飛龍院、幸開封府、幸都亭驛、幸禮賢院、幸茶庫染院、幸河倉、幸金 鳳園，皆一再至焉。

translations.literal: Thereafter viewing naval drill twenty-eight times; visiting the Great Xiangguo Temple and Fengchan Temple five each; Dragon Rise Temple and the imperial younger brother’s Kaifeng prefectural garden three each; Great Pure Temple and Jianlong Temple twice each; Chongxia, Guanghua, and Dengjue temples once each; viewing water mills eight times; reviewing catapults, viewing water tanks, viewing the harvest, visiting Flying Dragon Courtyard, Kaifeng prefecture, Capital Pavilion post, Hall of Honoring Worthies, tea warehouse dyeing office, river warehouse, Golden Phoenix Garden—all once or twice.
translations.idiomatic: Later: twenty-eight naval drills; Great Xiangguo and Fengchan five each; Dragon Rise and the imperial brother’s garden three each; Great Pure and Jianlong twice; other temples once; water mills eight times; catapults, water tanks, harvest, Flying Dragon, Kaifeng, Capital Pavilion, Honoring Worthies, tea warehouse, river warehouse, Golden Phoenix—once or twice each.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國二年二月，幸新鑿池，賜役卒錢布有差，六月，幸飛龍院。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Taiping Xingguo of Taizong, he visited the newly dug pool and bestowed money and cloth on laborers by rank; in the sixth month he visited Flying Dragon Courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, Taiping Xingguo 2, second month: new pool with rewards to laborers; sixth month: Flying Dragon Courtyard.

sentences.zh: 是後凡四幸。

translations.literal: Thereafter four visits in all.
translations.idiomatic: Four visits followed.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，觀刈麥。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, he viewed wheat harvest.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, fourth month: wheat harvest viewing.

sentences.zh: 九年正月六日，幸景龍 門外水磑，帝臨水而坐，召從臣觀之，因謂曰：「此水出於山源，清澄甘潔。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the first month of the ninth year, he visited the water mill outside the Bright Dragon Gate; the emperor sat by the water and summoned attending officials to view, saying: “This water comes from a mountain source, clear, pure, and sweet.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, first month, day 6: water mill outside Bright Dragon Gate; the emperor said the stream was mountain-fed, clear and sweet.

sentences.zh: 近河之地，水味皆甘，豈河潤所及乎？」

translations.literal: In lands near the river the water’s taste is all sweet—is it because the river’s moisture reaches them?”
translations.idiomatic: Near the river all water tastes sweet—does the river’s moisture reach that far?”

sentences.zh: 宋琪等曰：「亦猶人性善惡，染習致然。」

translations.literal: Song Qi and others said: “It is also like human nature good and evil—habit and influence make it so.”
translations.idiomatic: Song Qi said: “Like human nature—habit shapes good and evil.”

sentences.zh: 帝 曰：「卿言是也。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Your statement is correct.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 四月，幸金明池習水戰，帝御水殿，召近臣觀之，謂宰相曰：「水戰，南方之事也。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he visited the Golden Bright Pond to practice naval warfare; the emperor attended the Water Hall and summoned close ministers to view, telling the chief counselor: “Naval warfare is a southern affair.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: Golden Bright Pond naval drill; at the Water Hall he told the counselor naval warfare was southern.

sentences.zh: 今其地已定，不復施用，時習之，示不忘戰耳。」

translations.literal: Now the territory is settled and will not again be applied; practicing from time to time shows not forgetting war.”
translations.idiomatic: The realm was settled, yet practice showed he had not forgotten war.”

sentences.zh: 因幸講武 台，閱諸軍都試，軍中之絕技者遞加賜賚。

translations.literal: He then visited the Martial Lecture Terrace and reviewed the various armies’ examinations; those with exceptional skills in the army were rewarded in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He then reviewed army examinations at the Martial Lecture Terrace and rewarded exceptional skills.

sentences.zh: 遂登瓊林苑樓，陳百戲，擲金錢，令樂人爭之，極歡而罷。

translations.literal: He then ascended the Jade Forest Garden tower, displayed the hundred entertainments, threw gold coins, and ordered musicians to compete for them, ending in utmost joy.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jade Forest tower he staged entertainments, threw gold coins for musicians, and ended in joy.

sentences.zh: 五月二日，出南薰門觀稼，召從臣列坐田中，令民刈麥，咸賜 以錢帛。

translations.literal: On the second day of the fifth month he went out the Southern Fragrant Gate to view the harvest, summoned attending officials to sit in rows in the field, ordered the people to reap wheat, and all were bestowed money and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month, day 2: he viewed harvest outside the Southern Fragrant Gate, sat officials among reapers, and rewarded farmers.

sentences.zh: 回幸玉津園觀漁，張樂、習射，既宴而歸。

translations.literal: Returning he visited the Jade Ford Garden to view fishing, played music, practiced archery, banqueted, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Returning through Jade Ford Garden he fished, shot, banqueted, and went home.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，幸城南觀麥，賜田夫布帛有差。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year he visited the south city to view wheat and bestowed cloth on field laborers by rank.
translations.idiomatic: Next year, fifth month: south-city wheat viewing with cloth for laborers.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年四月，幸金明池觀水嬉，賜從官飲。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the fourth year of Yongxi, he visited the Golden Bright Pond to view water games and bestowed drink on attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi 4, fourth month: Golden Bright Pond water games with drink for attendants.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「雨霽天涼，中 外無事，宜勿惜醉。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: “Rain has cleared and the sky is cool; inside and outside there are no affairs—you should not spare getting drunk.”
translations.idiomatic: He said: “The rain has cleared, all is calm—do not spare drunkenness.”

sentences.zh: 因登苑中樓，盡歡而罷。

translations.literal: He then ascended a tower in the garden and ended in full joy.
translations.idiomatic: He ascended a garden tower and ended in full joy.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年三月，幸金明池，命為競渡之戲，擲銀甌於波間，令人泅波取之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the third year of Chunhua, he visited the Golden Bright Pond and ordered competitive crossing games; he threw a silver bowl into the waves and had men swim to fetch it.
translations.idiomatic: Chunhua 3, third month: competitive crossing at Golden Bright Pond with a silver bowl thrown for swimmers.

sentences.zh: 因御船奏教坊樂，岸上都人縱觀者萬計。

translations.literal: He then attended in the imperial boat while the Music Office played; on the shore the capital’s people numbering ten thousand all viewed.
translations.idiomatic: He boated while the Music Office played before tens of thousands on shore.

sentences.zh: 帝顧視高年皓首者，就賜白金器皿。

translations.literal: The emperor looked at the elderly with white hair and bestowed platinum vessels on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: He bestowed platinum vessels to white-haired elders he noticed.

sentences.zh: 九月，幸潛龍園，駐輦池東岸，臨水謂近臣曰：「朕不至此已十年，昔尹京日，無事常痛飲池上，今池邊之木已成林矣。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month he visited the Hidden Dragon Garden, halted the carriage east of the pond bank, faced the water and told close ministers: “I have not come here in ten years; when I administered the capital I often drank deeply on the pond—now the trees by the pond have become a forest.”
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Hidden Dragon Garden; he said he had not come in ten years and the pondside trees were now a forest.

sentences.zh: 因顧 教坊使郭守忠等數人曰：「汝等前日以樂童從我，今亦皓首，光陰迅速如此。」

translations.literal: He then looked at Music Office Commissioner Guo Shouzhong and several others and said: “You formerly followed me as music boys; now you too are white-haired—time passes so swiftly.”
translations.idiomatic: He told Guo Shouzhong and others they had once been his music boys and were now white-haired.

sentences.zh: 嗟歎久之。

translations.literal: He sighed long.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 帝親引滿舉白，群臣盡醉。

translations.literal: The emperor personally filled and raised the white goblet; the ministers were all drunk.
translations.idiomatic: He filled the white goblet himself; all ministers were drunk.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平元年八月，幸諸王宮。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xianping of Zhenzong, he visited the various princes’ palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong, Xianping 1, eighth month: princes’ palaces.

sentences.zh: 二年九月，幸開寶寺、福聖院。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the second year, he visited Kaibao Temple and Fusheng Courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, ninth month: Kaibao Temple and Fusheng Courtyard.

sentences.zh: 是後，二寺臨幸者凡十有四。

translations.literal: Thereafter visits to the two temples totaled fourteen.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen visits to those two temples followed.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，幸金明池觀水戲，揚旗鳴鼓，分左右翼，植木係彩，以為標識，方舟疾進，先至者賜之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, he visited the Golden Bright Pond to view water games; flags were raised and drums sounded; left and right wings were deployed; wooden posts with colored silk were set as markers; swift boats raced forward and the first to arrive was rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, fifth month: Golden Bright Pond naval games with wing divisions, markers, and rewards to winners.

sentences.zh: 移 幸瓊林苑，登露台，鈞容直奏樂，台下百戲競集，從臣皆醉。

translations.literal: He moved to visit the Jade Forest Garden, ascended the open terrace; the Imperial Music Band played; below the terrace the hundred entertainments gathered; attending officials were all drunk.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Jade Forest Garden, ascended the terrace to music and entertainments; attendants were drunk.

sentences.zh: 自是凡四臨幸。

translations.literal: From this there were four visits in all.
translations.idiomatic: Four such visits followed.

sentences.zh: 九月，幸大相國寺。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, he visited the Great Xiangguo Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: Great Xiangguo Temple.

sentences.zh: 是後再幸者九。

translations.literal: Thereafter nine more visits.
translations.idiomatic: Nine more visits followed.

sentences.zh: 幸上清宮者十有二，幸玉津園者十，幸太一宮、玉 清昭應宮各六，餘不盡載。

translations.literal: Visits to the Upper Pure Palace twelve; Jade Ford Garden ten; Great Unity Temple and Jade Clarity Responding Palace six each; the rest not all recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Upper Pure Palace twelve times; Jade Ford ten; Great Unity and Jade Clarity Responding Palace six each; others not fully recorded.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年正月十九日，中書門下上言：「伏睹今月十四日，皇帝詣諸宮寺焚香，總三十餘處，過百拜以上。

translations.literal: On the nineteenth day of the first month of the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu, the Secretariat and Chancellery submitted: “We observe that on the fourteenth of this month the emperor went to various palace temples to burn incense, altogether more than thirty places, over a hundred bows.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong Xiangfu 8, first month, day 19: Secretariat reported the emperor had burned incense at more than thirty temples on the fourteenth, bowing over a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 臣等侍從，倍增憂灼，昨 崇政殿已麵奏陳。

translations.literal: Your ministers attending were increasingly anxious; yesterday this was already memorialized face-to-face at the Chongzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Attending ministers were deeply anxious and had already memorialized at Chongzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 臣聞尊事萬靈，固先精意；

translations.literal: Your minister hears that honoring the ten thousand spirits must first concentrate the mind;
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the spirits requires concentrated mind;

sentences.zh: 登用百禮，乃貴時中。

translations.literal: employing the hundred rites must value timeliness.
translations.idiomatic: employing the hundred rites requires proper timing.

sentences.zh: 在經久之從宜，必裁正而惟允。

translations.literal: What long follows expedience must be corrected to be solely proper.
translations.idiomatic: Long-standing expedients must be corrected to proper form.

sentences.zh: 伏望特命攸司，載詳定式。

translations.literal: I humbly hope specially to order the relevant office to examine in detail and fix the pattern.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask the relevant office to fix the pattern in detail.

sentences.zh: 自今車駕幸諸宮、觀、寺、院，正殿 再拜；

translations.literal: From now when the imperial carriage visits various palaces, temples, and abbeys, bow twice in the main hall;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth at palace and temple visits: two bows in the main hall;

sentences.zh: 及諸殿，令群臣以下分拜。

translations.literal: at the various halls, order ministers and below to divide and bow.
translations.idiomatic: at subsidiary halls ministers and below bow separately.

sentences.zh: 庶垂億載，允葉通規。」

translations.literal: May this be handed down for ten thousand ages and accord with the universal rule.
translations.idiomatic: May this endure for ages as universal rule.

sentences.zh: 乃詔禮儀院詳定差減焉。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered the Ritual Institute to examine in detail and reduce.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Ritual Institute to revise and reduce the bows.

sentences.zh: 仁宗景祐三年，詔閣門詳定車駕幸宮、觀、寺、院支賜茶絹等第。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jingyou of Renzong, an edict ordered the Gate Office to fix in detail the grades of bestowed tea and silk when the imperial carriage visited palaces, temples, and abbeys.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong, Jingyou 3: the Gate Office fixed grades of tea and silk bestowed on palace and temple visits.

sentences.zh: 哲宗紹聖四年三月八日，詔自今遇車駕出新城，令殿前馬、步軍司取旨，權差馬、步軍赴新城外四面巡檢下祗應，每壁馬軍二百人，步軍三百人，並於城外巡警。

translations.literal: On the eighth day of the third month of the fourth year of Shaosheng of Zhezong, an edict: from now when the imperial carriage goes out to the new city, order the Palace Front and Rear Guard Service to take instructions and temporarily detail horse and foot troops to patrol outside the new city on four sides for attendance; on each wall 200 horse troops and 300 foot troops, all patrolling outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhezong, Shaosheng 4, third month, day 8: when the emperor went to the new city, horse and foot guards patrolled outside—200 horse and 300 foot per wall.

sentences.zh: 三元觀燈，本起於方外之說。

translations.literal: Triple Origin lantern viewing originally arose from non-Buddhist teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Triple Origin lantern viewing began as a non-Buddhist custom.

sentences.zh: 自唐以後，常於正月望夜，開坊市門然燈。

translations.literal: From the Tang afterward, on the night of the full moon of the first month they regularly opened ward and market gates to light lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tang, the first-month full moon regularly opened markets for lanterns.

sentences.zh: 宋因之，上元前後各一日，城中張燈，大內正門結彩為山樓影燈，起露台，教坊陳百戲。

translations.literal: The Song followed this; one day before and after the Upper Yuan, lanterns were hung in the city; at the great inner main gate a colored mountain-pavilion shadow lantern was erected and an open terrace raised; the Music Office displayed the hundred entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: Song followed: around Upper Yuan the city was lit; the inner gate had a mountain lantern and terrace; the Music Office staged entertainments.

sentences.zh: 天子先幸寺觀行香，遂禦樓，或禦東華門及東西角樓，飲從臣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven first visited temples to burn incense, then attended the tower, or attended the Eastern Flowery Gate and the east and west corner towers, and drank with attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first burned incense at temples, then viewed lanterns from a tower or the Eastern Flowery Gate and corner towers, drinking with attendants.

sentences.zh: 四夷蕃客各依本國歌舞列於樓下。

translations.literal: Four-foreign and tribal guests each according to their state’s songs and dances lined below the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign guests performed their native songs and dances below the tower.

sentences.zh: 東華、左右掖門、東西角樓、城門大道、大宮觀寺院，悉起山棚， 張樂陳燈，皇城雉堞亦遍設之。

translations.literal: The Eastern Flowery, left and right side gates, east and west corner towers, great gate roads, great palace temples and abbeys—all raised lantern sheds; music was spread and lanterns hung; the imperial city battlements were also fully set.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Flowery Gate, side gates, corner towers, avenues, and temples all had lantern sheds and music; even the city walls were lit.

sentences.zh: 其夕，開舊城門達旦，縱士民觀。

translations.literal: That evening the old city gates were opened until dawn, and commoners were allowed to view.
translations.idiomatic: That night old city gates stayed open until dawn for commoners to view.

sentences.zh: 後增至十七、十八夜。

translations.literal: Later it was increased to seventeen and eighteen nights.
translations.idiomatic: Later the festival grew to seventeen or eighteen nights.

sentences.zh: 太祖建隆二年上元節，禦明德門樓觀燈，召宰相、樞密、宣徽、三司使、端明、翰林、樞密直學士、兩省五品以上官、見任前任節度觀察使飲宴，江南、吳越朝貢使預焉。

translations.literal: On the Upper Yuan of the second year of Jianlong of Taizu, he attended the Bright Virtue Gate tower to view lanterns, summoned chief counselor, Bureau, Palace Domestic Service, Three Departments commissioner, Duanming, Hanlin, Bureau direct academicians, Secretariat and Chancellery fifth rank and above, current and former military commissioners and observation commissioners to drink; Jiangnan and Wuyue tribute envoys also participated.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, Jianlong 2, Upper Yuan: he viewed lanterns from Bright Virtue Gate tower and feasted counselors, scholars, commissioners, and Jiangnan and Wuyue envoys.

sentences.zh: 四夷蕃客列坐樓下，賜酒食勞之，夜分而罷。

translations.literal: Four-foreign and tribal guests sat in rows below the tower; drink and food were bestowed to comfort them; at midnight it ended.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign guests sat below the tower, were given food and drink, and the night ended at midnight.

sentences.zh: 三年正月十三夜然燈，罷內前排場戲樂，以昭憲皇太后喪製故也。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth night of the first month of the third year lanterns were lit; inner front stage entertainments were canceled because of mourning regulations for Empress Zhaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, first month, night 13: lanterns were lit but inner entertainments canceled for Empress Zhaoxian’s mourning.

sentences.zh: 太平興國二年七月中元節，禦東角樓觀燈，賜從官宴飲。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the second year of Taiping Xingguo, on the Zhongyuan festival, he attended the Eastern Corner Tower to view lanterns and bestowed drink on attending officials.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping Xingguo 2, seventh month, Zhongyuan: Eastern Corner Tower lantern viewing with drink for attendants.

sentences.zh: 五年十月下元節，依中元例，張燈三夜。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year, on the Xiayuan festival, following the Zhongyuan precedent, lanterns were hung for three nights.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, tenth month, Xiayuan: three nights of lanterns like Zhongyuan.

sentences.zh: 雍熙五年上元節，不觀燈，躬耕籍田故也。

translations.literal: On the Upper Yuan of the fifth year of Yongxi, lanterns were not viewed because he personally plowed the sacred field.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi 5, Upper Yuan: no lanterns because of sacred-field plowing.

sentences.zh: 後凡遇用兵及災變、諸臣之喪，皆罷。

translations.literal: Later whenever there was military use or disasters and changes, or mourning for various ministers, all were canceled.
translations.idiomatic: Later war, disasters, or ministers’ mourning canceled the festival.

sentences.zh: 政和三年正月，詔放燈五日。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Zhenghe, an edict released lanterns for five days.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghe 3, first month: lanterns for five days.

sentences.zh: 五年十二月二十九日，詔景龍門預為元夕之具，實欲觀民風、察時態、黼飾太平、增光樂國，非徒以遊豫為事。

translations.literal: On the twenty-ninth day of the twelfth month of the fifth year, an edict: the Bright Dragon Gate was prepared beforehand for the Yuanxi lanterns—truly to observe the people’s customs, survey the times, adorn peace, and increase the rejoicing nation, not merely to make excursion and pleasure the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, twelfth month, day 29: Bright Dragon Gate preparations were said to observe customs and adorn peace, not mere pleasure.

sentences.zh: 特賜公、師、宰執以 下宴，及御製詩四韻賜太師蔡京。

translations.literal: Specially bestowed a banquet to dukes, grandees, and chief counselors and below, and an imperial poem of four rhymes bestowed on Grand Preceptor Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He banqueted dukes and counselors and gave a four-rhyme poem to Grand Preceptor Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 六年正月七日，御筆：「今歲閏餘候晚，猶未春和。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the first month of the sixth year, imperial brush: “This year the intercalary surplus makes the season late; spring harmony is not yet here.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, first month, day 7: imperial note: the intercalary year delays spring.

sentences.zh: 晷短氣寒，於宴集無舒緩之樂。

translations.literal: The days are short and the air cold; at banquet gatherings there is no relaxed joy.
translations.idiomatic: Short days and cold air make banquets less joyful.

sentences.zh: 景靈宮朝獻，移十四日東宮、十五日西宮， 畢，詣上清儲祥宮燒香。

translations.literal: Jingling Palace audience was moved to the fourteenth for the Eastern Palace and fifteenth for the Western Palace; when finished, go to the Upper Pure Stored Auspice Palace to burn incense.
translations.idiomatic: Jingling audiences moved to the 14th and 15th; then incense at Upper Pure Stored Auspice Palace.

sentences.zh: 十六日詣醴泉觀等處燒香。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth go to the Sweet Spring Abbey and other places to burn incense.
translations.idiomatic: On the 16th incense at Sweet Spring Abbey and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 上元節移於閏正月十四日為始。」

translations.literal: The Upper Yuan festival was moved to begin on the fourteenth of the intercalary first month.
translations.idiomatic: Upper Yuan began on intercalary first month, day 14.

sentences.zh: 宣和六年十二月二十四日，賜太師蔡京以下應兩府赴睿謨殿宴，景龍門觀燈。

translations.literal: On the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month of the sixth year of Xuanhe, Grand Preceptor Cai Jing and those below who should attend the two administrations were banqueted at the Bright Exposition Hall; Bright Dragon Gate lantern viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhe 6, twelfth month, day 24: Cai Jing and the two administrations banqueted at Bright Exposition Hall, then Bright Dragon lanterns.

sentences.zh: 續有旨，宣太傅王黼赴宴。

translations.literal: A further edict summoned Grand Tutor Wang Fu to the banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Wang Fu was also summoned.

sentences.zh: 七年正月十八日，宴輔臣，觀燈。

translations.literal: On the eighteenth day of the first month of the seventh year, he banqueted assisting ministers and viewed lanterns.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, first month, day 18: ministers banqueted and lanterns viewed.

sentences.zh: 賜酺。

translations.literal: Bestowed communal feast.
translations.idiomatic: Bestowed communal feast.

sentences.zh: 自秦始。

translations.literal: From the Qin it began.
translations.idiomatic: It began in the Qin.

sentences.zh: 秦法，三人以上會飲則罰金，故因事賜酺，吏民會飲，過則禁之。

translations.literal: Qin law: when three or more gathered to drink there was a fine in gold; therefore on occasions communal drinking was bestowed, officials and people gathered to drink, and excess was forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Qin law fined gatherings of three or more drinkers, so the throne bestowed communal feasts while forbidding unsanctioned drinking.

sentences.zh: 唐嘗一再舉行。

translations.literal: The Tang once or twice held it.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang held it only occasionally.

sentences.zh: 太宗雍熙元年十二月，詔曰：「王者賜酺推思，與眾共樂，所以表升平之盛事，契億兆之歡心。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the first year of Yongxi of Taizong, an edict said: “The king bestows communal drinking to extend grace and share joy with the multitude—therefore to display the flourishing event of rising peace and join the hearts of the hundred million.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, Yongxi 1, twelfth month: an edict said communal feasts extend grace and display rising peace to join all hearts.

sentences.zh: 累朝以來，此事久廢，蓋逢多故，莫舉舊章。

translations.literal: Through successive reigns this affair had long been abandoned, mostly encountering many troubles and not raising the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Successive reigns had abandoned it amid troubles.

sentences.zh: 今四海混同，萬民康 泰，嚴禋始畢，慶澤均行。

translations.literal: Now the four seas are united, the ten thousand people are secure and prosperous; solemn sacrifice has just been completed and celebratory favor is equally extended.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm was united, the people secure, and sacrifice complete—celebration could be shared.

sentences.zh: 宜令士庶之情，共慶休明之運，可賜酺三日。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to let the feelings of scholars and commoners together celebrate the brilliant fortune; communal drinking may be bestowed for three days.”
translations.idiomatic: Commoners and officials alike should celebrate—communal drinking was bestowed for three days.”

sentences.zh: 二十一日，禦丹鳳樓觀酺，召侍臣賜飲。

translations.literal: On the twenty-first day he attended the Cinnabar Phoenix Tower to view the communal feast, summoned attending officials and bestowed drink.
translations.idiomatic: Day 21: Cinnabar Phoenix Tower communal feast viewing with drink for attendants.

sentences.zh: 自樓前至朱雀門張樂，作山車、旱船，往來禦 道。

translations.literal: From before the tower to the Vermilion Bird Gate music was played; mountain carts and land boats moved along the imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: Music ran from the tower to Vermilion Bird Gate with mountain carts and land boats on the imperial road.

sentences.zh: 又集開封府諸縣及諸軍樂人列於禦街，音樂雜發，觀者溢道，縱士庶遊觀，遷市肆百貨於道之左右。

translations.literal: Also gathered Kaifeng prefecture counties and various army musicians in rows on the imperial street; music mixed and issued; viewers filled the road; commoners were allowed to view; market shops and goods were moved to both sides of the road.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng and army musicians lined the street; crowds filled the road and shops moved aside.

sentences.zh: 召畿甸耆老列坐樓下，賜之酒食。

translations.literal: He summoned capital-district elders to sit in rows below the tower and bestowed drink and food.
translations.idiomatic: Capital elders sat below the tower and received food and drink.

sentences.zh: 明日，賜群臣宴於尚書 省，仍作詩以賜。

translations.literal: The next day he bestowed a banquet on the ministers at the Secretariat and also composed a poem to bestow.
translations.idiomatic: Next day ministers banqueted at the Secretariat and received an imperial poem.

sentences.zh: 明日，又宴群臣，獻歌、詩、賦、頌者數十人。

translations.literal: The next day again he banqueted the ministers; those presenting songs, poems, rhapsodies, and eulogies numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: The following day another ministerial banquet brought dozens of poems and songs.

sentences.zh: 真宗景德三年九月，詔許群臣、士庶選勝宴樂，御史臺、皇城司毋得糾察。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the third year of Jingde of Zhenzong, an edict permitted ministers, scholars, and commoners to choose scenic places for banquets and music; the Censorate and Imperial City Service were not to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong, Jingde 3, ninth month: officials and commoners could feast freely without censor investigation.

sentences.zh: 四年二月 甲申，上御五鳳樓觀酺，宗室、近臣侍坐。

translations.literal: On the day jiashen of the second month of the fourth year, the emperor attended the Five Phoenix Tower to view the communal feast; imperial clan and close ministers sat in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, second month, jiashen: Five Phoenix Tower communal feast with clan and close ministers.

sentences.zh: 樓前露台奏教坊樂，召父老五百人列坐，賜飲於樓下。

translations.literal: Before the tower the open terrace played Music Office music; five hundred elders were summoned to sit in rows and were bestowed drink below the tower.
translations.idiomatic: Music played on the terrace; five hundred elders drank below the tower.

sentences.zh: 後二日，上復禦樓，賜宗室、文武百官宴於都亭驛，賜諸班、諸軍 將校羊酒。

translations.literal: Two days later the emperor again attended the tower and bestowed a banquet on imperial clan and civil and military officials at the Capital Pavilion post; all ranks and various army commanders were bestowed lamb and wine.
translations.idiomatic: Two days later clan and officials banqueted at Capital Pavilion and commanders received lamb and wine.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符元年正月，詔應致仕官並令赴都亭驛酺宴，禦樓日合預坐者亦聽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dazhong Xiangfu, an edict ordered retired officials also to attend the Capital Pavilion communal feast; on imperial tower day those who should sit were also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong Xiangfu 1, first month: retired officials could attend Capital Pavilion communal feasts.

sentences.zh: 又詔朝臣已辭、未見，並聽赴會。

translations.literal: Also an edict: court officials who had resigned but not yet been received were also permitted to attend.
translations.idiomatic: Resigned officials not yet received at court could also attend.

sentences.zh: 凡酺，命內諸司使三人主其事，於乾元樓前 露台上設教坊樂。

translations.literal: For communal feasts, three inner palace service commissioners were ordered to manage the affair; on the open terrace before the Qianyuan Tower the Music Office was set.
translations.idiomatic: Three inner commissioners managed communal feasts with Music Office on the Qianyuan Tower terrace.

sentences.zh: 又駢係方車四十乘，上起彩樓者二，分載鈞容直、開封府樂。

translations.literal: Also forty square carts were yoked in parallel; two raised colored towers, separately carrying the Imperial Music Band and Kaifeng prefecture musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Forty square carts included two colored towers for the Imperial Band and Kaifeng musicians.

sentences.zh: 復為棚車二十四，每十二乘為之，皆駕以牛，被之錦繡，縈以彩紖，分載諸軍、京畿 伎樂，又於中衢編木為欄處之。

translations.literal: Again twenty-four shed carts, each twelve yoked, all driven by oxen, covered in brocade, bound with colored cords, separately carrying various armies and capital-region entertainers; also in the middle avenue wooden fences were woven to place them.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-four brocade-covered ox carts carried army and capital entertainers in fenced ranks along the avenue.

sentences.zh: 徙坊市邸肆對列御道，百貨駢布，競以彩幄鏤版為飾。

translations.literal: Ward market shops were moved to face each other along the imperial road; goods crowded in abundance, competing to use colored tents and carved panels as ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Shops lined the imperial road under colored tents and carved panels.

sentences.zh: 上御乾元門，召京邑父老分番列坐樓下，傳旨問安否，賜以衣服、茶帛。

translations.literal: The emperor attended the Qianyuan Gate, summoned capital fathers and elders in turns to sit in rows below the tower, transmitted an edict asking after their well-being, and bestowed clothes, tea, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: At Qianyuan Gate elders sat below the tower, were greeted by edict, and received clothes, tea, and silk.

sentences.zh: 若五 日，則第一日近臣侍坐，特召丞、郎、給、諫，上舉觴，教坊樂作，二大車自升平橋而北，又有旱船四挾之以進，朋車由東西街交騖，並往復日再焉。

translations.literal: If five days, then on the first day close ministers attended seated; specially summoned directors, regular directors, remonstrance and memorial officials; the emperor raised his goblet; the Music Office played; two great carts came north from Shengping Bridge; also four land boats advanced flanking them; pleasure carts raced east and west streets, all going and returning twice a day.
translations.idiomatic: On five-day feasts day one seated close ministers and directors; great carts and land boats paraded from Shengping Bridge twice daily.

sentences.zh: 東距望春門， 西連閶闔門，百戲競作，歌吹騰沸。

translations.literal: East reaching Spring View Gate, west connecting to Peaceful Gate; the hundred entertainments competed; songs and pipes surged.
translations.idiomatic: From Spring View Gate to Peaceful Gate entertainments and music surged.

sentences.zh: 宗室親王、近列牧伯洎舊臣、宗室官，為設彩棚於左右廊廡。

translations.literal: Imperial clan princes, close frontier governors, and old ministers and clan officials had colored sheds set in the left and right corridors.
translations.idiomatic: Princes, frontier governors, and clan officials had colored sheds in the corridors.

sentences.zh: 士庶縱觀，車騎填溢，歡呼震動。

translations.literal: Scholars and commoners viewed freely; carriages and horsemen filled and overflowed; shouts shook the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Crowds filled the streets and shouts shook the ground.

sentences.zh: 第二日宴群臣百官於都亭驛、宗 室於親王宮。

translations.literal: The second day banqueted the hundred officials at the Capital Pavilion post and the imperial clan at the princes’ palace.
translations.idiomatic: Day two: officials at Capital Pavilion, clan at princes’ palace.

sentences.zh: 第三日宴宗室內職於都亭驛、近臣於宰相第。

translations.literal: The third day banqueted inner-clan officials at the Capital Pavilion and close ministers at the chief counselor’s residence.
translations.idiomatic: Day three: inner clan at Capital Pavilion, close ministers at the counselor’s house.

sentences.zh: 第四日宴百官於都亭驛、宗室於外苑。

translations.literal: The fourth day banqueted the hundred officials at the Capital Pavilion and the imperial clan at the outer garden.
translations.idiomatic: Day four: officials at Capital Pavilion, clan in the outer garden.

sentences.zh: 第五日復宴宗室內職於都亭驛、近臣於外苑。

translations.literal: The fifth day again banqueted inner-clan officials at the Capital Pavilion and close ministers in the outer garden.
translations.idiomatic: Day five: inner clan at Capital Pavilion, close ministers in the outer garden.

sentences.zh: 上多作詩，賜令屬 和，及別為勸酒詩。

translations.literal: The emperor often composed poems, bestowed them ordering matching pieces, and separately made urging-wine poems.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often composed poems for matching and separate urging-wine verses.

sentences.zh: 禁軍將校日會於殿前馬、步軍之廨。

translations.literal: Palace guard commanders daily met at the hall-front horse and foot army offices.
translations.idiomatic: Guard commanders met daily at the horse and foot army halls.

sentences.zh: 是歲，東封泰山，所過州府，上御子城門樓，設山車、彩船載樂，從臣侍坐，本州父老、進奉 使、蕃客悉預。

translations.literal: That year, on the eastern Feng and Shan at Mount Tai, at each prefecture passed through the emperor attended the inner city gate tower, set mountain carts and colored boats carrying music; attending ministers sat; local elders, tribute envoys, and tribal guests all participated.
translations.idiomatic: That year’s eastern Feng and Shan: at each prefecture the emperor viewed from the inner gate tower with music carts; elders, tribute envoys, and tribal guests attended.

sentences.zh: 兗州駐蹕，仍賜群臣會於延壽寺。

translations.literal: At Yanzhou during the imperial halt he still bestowed a gathering for the ministers at the Longevity Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanzhou he banqueted ministers at Longevity Temple.

sentences.zh: 所在改賜門名，兗州曰「回鑾覃慶」，鄆州曰「升中延福」，濮州曰「告成延慶」。

translations.literal: Where he arrived gate names were changed and bestowed: Yanzhou “Return of the Carriage Extending Celebration,” Yunzhou “Ascending the Middle Extending Blessing,” Puzhou “Reporting Completion Extending Celebration.”
translations.idiomatic: Gates were renamed: Yanzhou Return Carriage Celebration, Yunzhou Ascending Middle Blessing, Puzhou Reporting Completion Celebration.

sentences.zh: 澶州以行宮迫隘，當衢結彩為 殿，名曰「延禧」。

translations.literal: At Danzhou the traveling palace was cramped; colored fabric was tied across the avenue as a hall named “Extending Celebration.”
translations.idiomatic: At Danzhou a cramped traveling palace became a colored “Extending Celebration” hall across the avenue.

sentences.zh: 幸汾陰、亳州，皆如東封路。

translations.literal: Visits to Fenyin and Bozhou all followed the eastern Feng and Shan route.
translations.idiomatic: Fenyin and Bozhou followed the eastern Feng and Shan route.

sentences.zh: 河中府門名曰「詔畢宣恩」，陝州曰「霈澤惠民」，鄭州曰「回鑾慶賜」。

translations.literal: Hezhong prefecture’s gate was named “Edict Completed Proclaiming Grace”; Shaanzhou “Great Favor Benefiting the People”; Zhengzhou “Return Carriage Celebration Bestowal.”
translations.idiomatic: Hezhong’s gate was Edict Completed Grace; Shaanzhou Great Favor for the People; Zhengzhou Return Carriage Bestowal.

sentences.zh: 西京將議改五鳳樓名，上曰：「此太祖 所建，因瑞應，不可更也。」

translations.literal: The Western Capital was about to discuss changing the Five Phoenix Tower name; the emperor said: “This was built by Taizu because of auspicious responses—it cannot be changed.”
translations.idiomatic: Changing the Western Capital’s Five Phoenix Tower was refused: Taizu built it for an omen and the name could not change.

sentences.zh: 華陰就行宮宴父老，賜驛亭名曰「宣澤」。

translations.literal: At Huayin he banqueted elders at the traveling palace and bestowed on the post pavilion the name “Proclaiming Moisture.”
translations.idiomatic: At Huayin he feasted elders and named the post pavilion Proclaiming Moisture.

sentences.zh: 至鄭州，以太宗忌日甫過，罷會，賜與如例。

translations.literal: At Zhengzhou, because Taizong’s death-day had just passed, the gathering was canceled but bestowals followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhengzhou the gathering was canceled for Taizong’s death-day but gifts followed precedent.

sentences.zh: 亳州曰「奉元均慶」，南京曰「重熙頒慶」。

translations.literal: Bozhou “Receiving the Origin Equal Celebration,” Nanjing “Repeated Radiance Issuing Celebration.”
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou received Receiving Origin Equal Celebration; Nanjing Repeated Radiance Issuing Celebration.

sentences.zh: 天禧五年，以畿縣追集、老人疲勞之故，止召兩赤縣、坊縣父老預會，其不預名亦聽，給以賜物。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxi, because capital counties were summoned and elders were wearied, only fathers and elders of the two red counties and ward counties were summoned to the gathering; those not on the list were also permitted and given bestowal goods.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi 5: to spare elders, only two red counties and ward counties were summoned, though others could still receive gifts.

sentences.zh: 天下賜酺，各令州、府會官屬父老，邊州或遣中使就賜。

translations.literal: Empire-wide bestowed communal feasts: each ordered prefectures and circuits to gather officials and elders; frontier prefectures sometimes sent eunuchs to bestow on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide communal feasts ordered each prefecture to gather officials and elders; frontiers might send eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 又詔開封府：「賜酺日，罪人酗酒而不傷人者，咸釋之。

translations.literal: Also an edict to Kaifeng prefecture: “On days of bestowed communal feast, criminals drunk but not harming people are all released.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng was told: on communal feast days non-violent drunkards were released.

sentences.zh: 再犯，論如法。」

translations.literal: If they offend again, punish according to law.”
translations.idiomatic: Repeat offenders were punished by law.”

sentences.zh: 後賜酺皆準此。

translations.literal: Later bestowed communal feasts all followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Later communal feasts followed this rule.

sentences.zh: 宋之繁庶，於斯為盛，後遂為定制雲。

translations.literal: Song’s prosperity and abundance at this point were at their height; afterward it became fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Song prosperity was then at its height, and this became fixed custom.
